Wang et al. 2610.06851, read in full (papers/arxiv-2610.06851.txt). (1) Their RL model is allenai/Olmo-3-7B-RL-Zero-Math (3.0 release, per their repo), not our Olmo-3.1. On MATH-500 at T 0.6 / top-p 0.95 / cap 31,744, 32 rollouts: base 42.2 -> cue 77.9 (Table 5); RL 75.0 -> 75.3 with cue (Table 6). So on their pair the cue already equals RL on MATH-500; our 10.6-point gap is against 3.1 only and is not in the paper. (2) DIRECTION.md says they report 77.7 for the cue: Table 5 says 77.9; 77.7 is the row 'RL opening + base continuation' (Table 13). (3) Their cue is 2 tokens ('.\n\n' + 'Okay'), chosen without labels by lowest answer entropy on 30 MATH train problems. (4) Cued base pass@16 on MATH-500 = 95.4 (Table 5), above our RL pass@1 of 92.6: the missing points are in the base's samples. (5) Harder sets: RL leads the cued base by 5-12 points (AMC 23 66.2 vs 59.5, AIME 2024 35.2 vs 23.3, OlympiadBench 41.6 vs 36.5), unexplained in the paper. (6) Not in the paper: any temperature sweep, restarts, base + a*(RL - base), a Code-RL model. 0 citing papers indexed on 2026-11-14. (7) Olmo 3 report 2512.13961 A.6.4: 3.1 differs from 3.0 by completion length 16k instead of 12k and by not masking truncated sequences (they are trained as negatives). work-2aaf3a

Published, do not run on a plain base (papers read in full, texts in papers/): (a) power sampling / MCMC: +2.4 to +3.5 points on MATH-500, 18-27 % of the RL gain, none on AIME (2610.24663 Table 1). (b) Fixed rules: forced 'Wait', logit bias, greedy first 100 tokens, entropy stop, longer prefill: at or below base (2610.24663 Tables 3, 5, App. G). (c) Majority vote: plain base stays below RL for 24 of 24 decoding policies at every N up to 16 on Qwen2.5-7B / MATH-500 (2609.01274 Fig. 8b). Maj@4 adds 0.8 points to a 73.6 % model on MATH500; best-of-n by self-confidence is below one sample (2507.18122 Table 1). (d) Loop penalties: DRY costs 14.2 points on MATH-500 for Qwen3-4B (2610.24715 Table 16). (e) Top-p vs temperature: removing top-p at T 0.6 cuts limit loops 59 -> 53, T 1 cuts to 24 (Qwen3-4B, 360 structured generations, not math; 2610.24715 Table 9). (f) RL gain is sparse: RL's greedy token at the 4 % of positions where greedy tokens differ recovers 90.5 % of the gain on AIME; base entropy finds those positions with AUROC 0.94-0.98; RL's token has mean rank 2.1-2.4 in the base (2610.24663 Table 3, App. E; 2605.06241 Table 2). No label-free rule is published that picks the right token there. (g) Label-free training (entropy minimization, vote reward) closes 80-100 % of the gap on Math-500 and 0-70 % on AIME for Qwen2.5-Math-7B (2505.15134 Table 2); vote reward collapses near 1,000 steps (2603.08660). None of (a)-(g) was run on a cued base or on the Olmo pair. work-2aaf3a

Double-check short answers at equal tokens (cued base, T 1.0). T1 data: base answers of <= 2,000 tokens are 263 of 500 and 13 are wrong; RL has 0 wrong among its 286 answers of <= 4,000 tokens. Procedure: when the first answer is <= 2,000 tokens, draw a second sample; if the two final answers differ, draw a third and take the majority. Cost ~514 extra tokens per problem, so base stays under RL's mean (3,933 + 514 vs 4,694). RL gets the same procedure (expected gain 0). Closest published: Maj@2/4 in 2507.18122 Table 1 and majority@k in 2610.06851 Fig. 21; differs in gating by length, matching tokens to RL, cued base. Refuted if fewer than 8 of the 13 are recovered (errors repeat across samples) or new errors offset them. Then the 328. From work-2aaf3a.

Stop at a length cutoff and restart (both models, T 1.0), cutoff chosen on MATH-500. T1: above 12,000 tokens the cued base has 15 right and 40 wrong answers; stopping there frees 329 tokens per problem. RL: 16 right, 22 wrong above 12,000. None of the base's 27 cap hits is a loop (rule A fires on 0 of 500): they are reasoning that does not converge, and RL solves 16 of them in a median of 8,594 tokens. The T 0.6 restart row recovered 60 of 119 cap hits. Closest published: 2601.11940 (restart at a matched budget of 4, UNREAD) and our K_fresh row; differs in T 1.0, cut by length instead of the cap, RL given the same rule, tokens counted. Refuted if the net gain at equal tokens is <= 0 for the base or equal for both models. From work-2aaf3a.

Disagreement map after the cue: score the existing 500 T1 and 500 T2 answers token by token under both models (teacher forcing, 4 passes, no sampling). Question: once the cue is given, where does Olmo-3.1 RL still disagree with the base? Prediction from the T1/T2 item table: on the base's 23 wrong answers under 4,000 tokens, RL gives low probability to the token where the base starts its final answer (RL has 0 wrong answers under 4,000 tokens and its right answers are 2.1x longer, median 3,014 vs 1,432). Closest published: 2610.24663 Table 3 and App. E, 2605.06241 Table 2 (Qwen pairs, plain base, no cue; RL differs at 1-4 % of positions). Differs in Olmo pair, cued prefix, the 3.1 model, and the test at the answer position. Refuted if RL's probability of the base's answer-start token is within 2x of the base's, or if disagreement is uniform over position. Also gives the per-position data for the weight-difference study. From work-2aaf3a.

Code-RL model on MATH-500 with and without the cue (one cell each, T 1.0): is the remaining 10.6 points specific to a math reward? 2610.06851 Table 6 has the reverse case only: the 3.0 Math-RL model scores 68.5 on HumanEval, cued base 69.8, base 50.2, and it has no Code-RL model. If Code-RL with the plain prompt is near 92 on MATH-500, the residual is task-general; if it is near the cued base (82), it is math-specific. This is the model-level version of the Code-RL control in the weight-difference study (idea-2eb58d) and costs 2 cells. Check the exact Code-RL model name on Hugging Face first. From work-2aaf3a.

Goodfire 'Neurons as an Interpretable Basis' (Nov 10 2026, goodfire.com/research/neurons-as-an-interpretable-basis), read in full by a subagent. Table 1/8 on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (MoE, SwiGLU): keeping only the top 320 of 4,096 routed MLP neuron activations per token and layer, with no training, raises loss 1.886 -> 1.940 (+2.9%) and raises MATH-500 from 69.8 by +5.8 (top-64: +7.0; resample noise +0.8) at a 4,096 thinking-token cap. Accuracy on items both arms finished is flat, so the gain is more answers finishing under the cap (subagent's inference). Other evals fell (GPQA-Diamond -11 to -18, MBPP+ -20) from looping and excess self-checking. Fig. 4: ablating all Q3 activations (gate<0 and up<0) cut GSM8K reasoning 1,550 -> 176 tokens. Single neurons control 'settle vs keep questioning' (L9_E98_N330). Their small RL recalibration 'mainly taught the model to commit and stop'. Not in the paper: any base-vs-fine-tune diff, any weight edit, any model near 7B. No code released.

Neuron-level route, literature state (19 Exa searches, 12 full reads, 2026-11-14): no paper diffs a base against its RL version in the MLP-neuron basis, transplants the top neurons and scores reasoning. For sparsity: Lu et al. 2611.10866, a reward-trained mask zeroing <0.05% of MLP gate weights matches full fine-tune (Qwen2.5-7B mean 52.3 vs 51.9, base 40.2; untrained Wanda mask at most 42.5); EdgeRunner 2606.13705, 1 to 1,062 neurons cut loops 46/384 -> 12/384 at T 0.7 with no measured regression; AdaRAS 2601.19847, label-ranked neuron steering MATH-500 84.8 -> 86.4. Against: Mukherjee 2505.11711, RL updates spread over all layers and matrices, near full rank; 2611.11752, OLMo-2-7B PPO update needs 2,120 of 4,096 components for 80% energy at L16 down-proj. Arora et al. 2601.22594 (RelP attribution, code github.com/TransluceAI/circuits): ~200 neurons give a faithful circuit for single-token tasks on Llama 3.1 8B. Local: studies/rlneurons/lib/n13_arms.py already builds neuron-transplant checkpoints (top 0.1/0.3/1/3% most-changed neurons moved to RL, energy-matched random controls, MLP-only, attention-only); the ranking driver and all arm scores are missing. Olmo 3 7B: 32 layers x 11,008 SwiGLU neurons = 352,256.

7 more papers read in full, 48 findings in past.dev (texts in papers/, gitignored; recall.py finds them). (a) 2510.14901 power sampling, Qwen2.5-Math-7B MATH500 1 sample: base 49.6, T 0.25 69.0, power 74.8, GRPO 78.5; 8.8x tokens, no equal-token baseline, cap 3,072, weak GRPO. Low T alone gives most of it (our cued Olmo loops at T 0.6). (b) 2506.15710 RAST: adding the 14B Zero-RL-minus-base logit difference at decode time lifts Qwen-2.5-32B MATH-500 68.6->80.7 vs its RL 81.3 (95%); base row greedy (confound); lambda >1 adds nothing; no random or wrong-domain control. (c) 2510.02611 temperature: base=RL only for oracle Pass@All (Qwen3-4B vs Polaris AIME25 27/30 each, ~15 T x 128 samples); RL leads at pass@1; no label-free pick. (d) 2505.17813 short-m@k: shortest of 20 chains 63.4 vs random 47.7 (LN-Super, T 0.7, 32k, capped excluded); short-3@k beats majority by 2-4 at equal tokens; length works only within a problem; reasoning models only. (e) 2505.11711: RL leaves 68.5-96% of weights unchanged at |d|<=1e-5 bf16 (52% at 1e-8, so partly rounding); update full-rank, uniform over layers -> random control must match per-matrix norm. (f) 2605.28751 weight extrapolation between two code-RL models: accuracy never rises past a=1; past ~1.5 answers run to the token cap (log length and cap rate); no random control. (g) 2610.39295 pass@k price: theorem on synthetic matrices only; on MATH-500 the cited real data has base never overtaking RL up to k=256. work-a028d2

Survey done, 4 scouts, 20 findings in past.dev. No published label-free weight method closes a ~10-pt RL gap at 7B (2609.18587 T2: vote-trained 77.0 vs RL 87.9, Qwen2.5-7B). J-lens workspace diff, base vs RL: teacher-force saved T1/T2 MATH-500 answers through both models, read mid-layer J-lens (fitted lens exists for base), list tokens RL holds that base lacks on the 65 RL-only problems vs 398 both-right. Forward only, ~1 H100-h. Null: shuffled pairs.

Lens-gated check cue: use the base's own J-lens readout to decide WHEN to insert a short check phrase (as the opening cue does once). Offline test first: does the readout predict positions where RL's token differs from base's better than output entropy? Refuted if AUROC <= entropy.

Workspace injection: add J-lens vectors of the RL-diff tokens to the base residual at workspace layers (38-92 % depth) during generation, 100 MATH-500 problems. Controls: norm-matched random direction, random-token lens vectors. Prior: lens writes are weak (19 % vs 75 % trained vectors).

Disagreement map, MATH-500, 500 T1 (base+cue) + 500 T2 (RL) answers scored under both Olmo models: the hypothesis 'RL refuses the token where the base starts a quick wrong answer' is REFUTED. D = ln P_RL - ln P_base at the base's answer-start token: wrong answers under 4,000 tokens median -0.53 (n=21), right answers of <= 2,000 tokens median -0.21 (n=250), permutation p = 0.82. D follows the answer format, not correctness: 'Answer:' line median -8.36 (n=132, 121 right), \boxed 0.000 (n=338); RL gives a wrong box the base's probability (median D 0.001, n=10). Top-1 tokens differ at 7.98 % of 1,966,404 T1 positions and 8.20 % of 2,346,899 T2 positions; the top 4 % of positions carry 38.7 % of KL (not sparse as in the 1-4 % published for greedy rollouts on Qwen pairs). Mean KL per token after the cue 0.06-0.09 nats; cue positions 8-12 nats. On the 16 cap hits RL's largest gaps are early (median relative position 0.19) and prefer ' Wait', ' too', ' Hmm'. At the base's true ends RL's P(stop) is below 0.5 in 16.5 % of 473 answers (base 4.2 %). Controls passed (base vs base KL 0, cue positions, calibration). From interp_research instruments E2 (a check of the Weight-Space Programming loop edit, complements knowledge-c9fc18 and result-6199f4): we re-ran the released Qwen3.5-0.8B edit (the editor's direction projected out of 64 MLP-out columns in each of layers 15 and 19, strength 6) beside random-column controls. 300 MATH-500 problems, one sample, 8,192-token cap, presence penalty 1.5. Accuracy: base 14/300 (4.7 %), released edit 33/300 (11.0 %), one random column set matched on weight norm 28/300 (9.3 %), one matched on KL 30/300 (10.0 %). Edit minus norm-matched random: +1.7 points [-1.7, +5.0], not separated. Cap hits: base 95 %, edit 88 %, random 90 %. The edit is specific on loops: the share of answers with a repeated 10-gram falls by 0.317 [0.247, 0.383] under the edit and by 0.08-0.09 under random columns. Columns ranked by alignment with the editor's direction reproduce it (64 columns 0.307, 256 columns 0.377), but that direction is the edit's own singular vector, so no weights-only discovery is shown. A KL-matched random control was no stricter than a norm-matched one. Status: exploratory; the frozen room gate cancelled every rule (cut share 0.96; the editor's own 32,768-token eval also cuts 93 % of base answers); one random draw only. Lesson for base + a*(RL - base) (work-d36669): on a cap-limited model a random edit of matched norm can give most of an accuracy gain; report a random-direction arm, cap hits and loops beside accuracy. cleanneurons Part T2 (attribution-ranked transplant), Olmo 3 base vs RL-Zero-Math: ranked by effect on 40 stored answers and scored on 40 held-out ones (2,672 decisive positions after the cue), the best 1 % of MLP neurons (3,523) copied from RL closes 13.7 % (T1 text) / 18.6 % (T2 text) of KL(RL||base); weight-change ranking 4.2 / 5.8 %, random 0.7 / 1.0 %. Best 0.1 % (352 neurons): 5.4 / 7.3 %. Best 10 %: 33.6 / 48.9 %. All MLP: 67.7 / 86.4 %. 88 % of all 352,256 neurons have a positive score, and the effects add up linearly: summed first-order scores predict a 0.542-nat drop, copying all MLP neurons gives 0.549 (of 0.708). So RL is a small, nearly linear nudge to almost every neuron; no small neuron set carries it, though the head is heavy (top 1 % = 19 % of the score). The best set sits in layers 1-15 (381 of 3,523 in layer 9) and layer 31. Hypothesis 'best 1 % closes >= 30 %' not met. Controls passed. Limit: teacher-forced distance to RL, not accuracy. From interp_research instruments (E1, E1b, E5, E6b; complements work-383069 and result-156f7b): on Olmo-3-1025-7B, writing a replacement value into a set of ~50 earlier-layer MLP neurons also moves a target neuron on contexts unrelated to that set, an off-target term absent in gemma and Qwen. Measured with 56 fake two-neuron pairs as the ratio of off-target fall to own fall (null should be 0): mean replacement 0.163 with all neurons eligible, 0.067 [0.034, 0.089] with the always-on neurons excluded; zero with exclusion 0.007 [-0.002, 0.032]; median 0.049; resample 0.147 (worst). Own falls are 0.42-0.48 under every value, so the value choice moves only the off-target part. gemma-3-4b-pt 0.004 and Qwen3-4B-Base 0.003 (no term). OLMo-2-1124-7B 0.123 [0.087, 0.169] against Olmo-3's 0.128 like for like: the term belongs to the OLMo lineage, not to Olmo-3's training run. Candidate causes, not separated: no input norms (output norms only), QK-norm over the whole projection, d 4096, MHA, untied embeddings. The term travels through the other window positions: writing only at the measured token leaves 0.005 [0.002, 0.010] against 0.074. Always-on neurons = top 1 % by mean activation (3,412); the ones that act are a few dozen mid-layer outliers at ~145x their layer's median |activation|. Rule for Olmo-3: zero (or write at the measured token only) with always-on neurons excluded; never mean replacement; on any OLMo model measure a random-set null first. Ablation results from Qwen or gemma papers do not transfer to Olmo without that null. Status: closed 2026-11-05, every stage read by a different model (errata E1b-b, E1b-f, E5-b, E6b-a to h). From interp_research mechanics (Olmo-3 internals; complements work-383069, relevant to the base's loops at T 0.6 in result-dadeec): on Olmo-3-1025-7B final weights, 512 repeated random-token sequences, 1,336 MLP neurons rise on the second pass by at least 0.2 of their 99.9th-percentile scale and 1,237 fall by as much (null max 0.055), about 2,600 of 352,256. 99.5 % sit at or after layer 7, the first induction-head layer (top detector head L15 H5); counts peak at layers 10-15 (121-171 per layer) with a second group of 60 in layers 29-31. Removing the top 8 induction heads leaves 0.771 [0.706, 0.839] of the top-100 neurons' repeat response (8 random heads leave 0.980), so the response is spread over more than 8 heads. The top-100 neurons' strongest corpus passages are literal repeats (text, code, repeated row formats) 8x [4, 12] as often as layer-matched random neurons' (0.16 vs 0.02). On rare random tokens the median neuron runs at 0.72 of its natural-text activity: 2.96x in layers 0-1, 0.36x in layers 26-31. Open: repetition not yet separated from predictability (erratum O-b; the control forward never ran). Status: closed; frozen R1 holds, R2 refuted on its point value, R3 holds, R4 cancelled (no room). From interp_research neuronoff (single-neuron ablation effect sizes; complements work-383069): zeroing one MLP neuron at one sign of its activation in Qwen3-4B-Base (156 neurons) and gemma-3-4b-pt (202) moves NLL on that neuron's own top contexts by a median 0.0026-0.0093 nats per side; the per-context median is at most 0.000037 nats. Zeroing a whole layer moves the median context by 0.014 (Qwen) and 0.021 (gemma) nats. The per-neuron positive control (a 0.05-nat floor) failed on 65/156 and 75/202 neurons, so every label was cancelled. Behaviour test on 7 hand-picked neurons: 0 of 7 changed generated text when zeroed. Status: closed and reviewed (a different model recomputed it from raw banks); cancelled by its own gate. Lesson: one neuron's necessity is about 0.01 nats on its own contexts, below a per-neuron floor of 0.05; a neuron-level test on Olmo-3 needs a pooled positive control checked for room, at least 30 held-out contexts per neuron, and the Olmo off-target null (instruments item). Artifact: interp_research studies/neuronoff/CLOSEOUT.md (claims N2, N12, N13), results/RESULTS.md section 3.

From interp_research bytegraft (scaling and sparse copies of a fine-tune weight difference; complements work-d36669, result-156f7b, work-f374ef): models Bolmo-1B-Stage1 (S), Bolmo-1B (F, S fine-tuned, has the skill) and OLMo-2-0425-1B (O); S's transformer body equals O's on all 176 tensors. Task: CUTE word and character edits, 1,200 items, exact match. (1) Dose curve O + lambda*(F - S) on the body, lambda 0.1 to 1.5: 23.50, 24.50, 25.25, 25.75, 27.08, 28.08, 28.75, 28.75, 27.92, 26.00 (lambda 1.0), 23.50, 15.75, 6.92, 3.75, 0.67 (O alone 22.00). Peak at lambda 0.7-0.8, not 1; past 1.1 the model collapses, and early end-of-text stops rise 5 (lambda 0.1) -> 152 (0.8) -> 181 (1.2). On S, lambda 0.5 gives 31.5 against S 23.83 and F 54.33 (25 % of the gain at half the dose). Lambda was picked on the scored items. (2) Sparse copies fail: a random 1 % of the difference scaled x100 and a random 0.1 % scaled x1000 (DARE-style) give 0/1,200; the 131 and 1,311 most-changed neurons with F's values give 22.67 and 20.00, below S's 23.83; random neurons dosed to the same realized change 24.08 and 9.42. (4) Adding the difference into a host unrelated to S (a checkpoint with weight cosine to O within +-0.002) gives 0.000 and degenerate text: adding a difference to an unrelated host breaks it and is not a transfer test (AUDIT d 8.7). From interp_research bytegraft (how small a fitted patch carries a skill, and whether an LLM editor finds it; complements result-6199f4 and knowledge-c9fc18): S = Bolmo-1B-Stage1 lacks a CUTE word-edit skill that its fine-tune Bolmo-1B has. On 2,400 held-out check items (S 14.42): a rank-1 LoRA fitted on all 112 matrices (753,664 numbers) reads 32.04 and beats an LLM editor's 8.5M-number neuron patch by +6.50 [4.83, 8.21]. LLM editor against a gradient-ranked neuron set of matched size: -0.75 [-2.71, 1.21]. At about 1M neurons the gradient ranking reads 22.12 and random neurons 18.08. The editor's +1.42 lead over a scripted top-32 falls to +0.46 [-0.71, 1.62] at a matched seed. LLM agents choosing attention heads to patch: 0.394 and 0.363 against gradient ranking 0.356 and a script given the same evidence table 0.375. No LLM-editor advantage over a gradient ranking or a script is shown; the gain comes from fitting, not from the chosen support: F's values copied onto the editor's or the gradient ranking's support with no fit lower the host (16.42 and 17.92 against 22.00). Character edits stay at 10 % or below under every patch. Transfer trap: a patch fitted without F still raises OLMo-2-0425-1B by +8.00, so 'patch transfers to another host' measured the shared interface, not the skill. Activation transfer: writing F's attention outputs into S recovers 0.81 of F's advantage (F's MLP writes none); controls (no-skill donor scaled to F's size 0.195, another item's writes 0.031) pass, but this is the donor running in parallel, not a weight graft. Status: closed, owner's verdict 'just LoRA'; audits AUDIT f, g, h, h2. Lesson for the RL gap: report a fitted low-rank arm and a gradient-ranked arm before crediting any hand- or LLM-chosen patch. Artifact: interp_research studies/bytegraft/results/arms_1m/arms_1m.json, GRAFT_closed.md, WRITEUP_2026-11-12.md, AUDIT_2026-11-11f.md to AUDIT_2026-11-12h2.md.

From interp_research next (20_ABSTRACT.md, 'The highest-leverage next step'; not run): rank test of the RL delta. For each MLP matrix of Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Math minus Olmo-3-1025-7B, add a rank-r truncation (SVD; r = 16, 64, 256) to the base, against a random subspace of equal rank and equal energy, MATH-500 (here: T 1.0, cue, run_cell.py; MLP-only so it compares with N13's whole-MLP arm, 86.4 at T 0.6), GSM8K held out on the rank-64 pair. Hypothesis: the gain sits in a low-rank part of each matrix's change (rank-64 within 2 SE of the whole-MLP arm). Refuted if rank-64 scores at the random-subspace control. Why now: N13 (knowledge-8229be) showed no neuron subset carries the gain but a 0.1 % DARE sample does; rank separates 'low-rank' from 'spread evenly'. Practical if it holds: r x (d+n) numbers per matrix for transplant or merging with the Code-RL delta. Cost estimate in the file: 6 arms, 12-16 GPU-h on L40S under N13's harness (SVD not costed); the same 6 arms on Modal H100 at T 1.0 are each one MATH-500 cell. Critique: priors point against low rank in energy (2505.11711: update nearly full rank; 2611.11752: OLMo-2-7B PPO update needs 2,120 of 4,096 components for 80 % energy at L16 down-proj), but energy rank is not functional rank, and 2605.21468 reports rank-1 trajectory extrapolation works. Also cited in interp_research next/04_RECENT.md, abstracts only: 2610.22438 (counted rank of 13 released fine-tuning updates up to 8B is only a little below a random matrix of the same shape) and 2609.22146 GRRR (removing the change of singular values keeps most math gains). WSP-1 (work-f374ef) computes singular spectra but does not score truncations. Use stochastic rounding into bf16 (work-d36669 found 54 % of delta entries <= 1 bf16 ulp).

From interp_research jmech (README.md, SPEC.md, results/run2/metrics.json): on the Olmo-3-1025-7B base, a J-lens swap of an entity written in the prompt works almost as well as editing the text, when clamped over a layer band. Status: open, not audited (no second reader).

Setup: model a81bae42, fp32; lens neuronpedia/jacobian-lens @d2527c3c (the file in knowledge-0220f1; its config sets no target layer, so it targets the final block). 8 countries x 4 relations (capital, language, continent, currency), prompts like 'Fact about {France}: the capital city of this country is'; 540 in-context terms. Edit = replace country s's two lens coordinates with country t's.
- Swap at every position, clamped over layers 12-29: the new country's answer rises 15.31 logits; replacing the word in the text gives 16.83 (91 %). Matched-norm random direction: 0.03 logits. Top-1 flips to t's answer in 519/540.
- Single-layer edit at the country token only: 5.83 logits at layer 6, 4.90 at L10, 4.46 at L14, 2.12 at L18, 0.35 at L22, 0.04 at L26 (of 32). Later positions have read the country by about layer 20.
- Not context-specific: the attributes the prompt does not ask for rise 0.56-0.60 times as much as the asked one (95 % CI about +-0.02, frozen label MIXED). Editing the text gives 0.53.
- The gradient (first-order) prediction holds only for small edits: ratio predicted/actual 0.76 (r 0.98) at strength 0.25, 0.10 (r 0.39) at strength 1.

For the team: the 'lens writes weakly' figure in result-da11d0 is for added vectors; replacing coordinates over a band of 18 layers moves a token-level variable almost fully. Set injection strength by measurement, not from the gradient. Cost: two runs of about 13 min on one RTX 6000 Ada, 0.54 USD (infra/vast/operations/2026-11-12_jmech.md).

In layers 24-31 on RL text, 49.5 % of neurons have r < 0.9 and median slope is 0.935; poles firing 2x more often in RL 8.0 %, 2x less 3.8 % (general text: 0 %). From interp_research rlneurons (RLN-4 loop detectors): use the zlib rule (rule A), not a period rule or a repeated-line count, to call base-model loops. Rule A: an 8,000-character window starting at a line start with zlib compression ratio < 0.10; onset = first line of the repeated block. Tested on saved MATH-500 answers (T 0.6, cap 16,384): fires on 0 of 484 RL finished answers, 1 of 431 base plain (n13), 0 of 435 and 0 of 381 for two base-01 cells; fires on 59 of 60, 46 of 48 and 90 of 92 low-ratio cap hits. Rule B (period <= 64 characters over >= 2,000 characters, 3 cycles; as relayed from arXiv 2611.06095, paper not read) has no false positives but catches only 6-17 % of the loops, because the base's loops have periods of hundreds of characters. A crude rule (any line > 20 characters three times) fires on 60 of 484 RL finished answers, so it fails. Caveat: on low-ratio cap hits rule A's hit rate is nearly guaranteed by construction; the test is the false-positive side, and the onset was checked by eye on 4 answers only. At T 1.0 rule A finds 0 loops in T1, T2 and T3 (500 each); the cued base at T 0.6 has 92 low-ratio cap hits of 119. Status: closed instrument check, not audited. Artifacts: interp_research-clean-neurons/studies/rlneurons/rln4/offline/prep_checks.json (detector), SPEC4.md section 4; code iterate-hack studies/rlneurons/lib/rln4_lib.py onset_lines.

On the 246 paired problems pass@4 is 157 for the base against 148 for RL single. A selector that needs no answer key and recovers half of the 26 problems between vote@4 and pass@4 would put the cued base at RL's level at 4x tokens. Rows exist (work-140e13). Literature from interp_research, 30 papers read in full, 147 findings in past.dev (recall.py). What bears on the direction: (1) RL gain is sparse in tokens and re-weights base behavior: swapping the RL token at 4-8% of positions lifts base AIME24 to RL level, RL token is in base top-3 >80% (2603.22446); RL keeps the base's forking positions, 86.7% overlap (2506.01939); base Olmo-3-7B already writes 'wait' ~5/1k, RL-Zero-Math 76.5/1k at T 0.6 with 29.1% length-limit hits vs 17.8% base (2610.30882); URIAL: 92% of chat tokens in base top-3, shift at the start (2312.01552). Spurious rewards help only where the behavior exists; OLMo2 flat (2506.10947). (2) Weight difference: rank-1 of the RL update, rescaled, keeps ~100% of MATH-500 gain, lambda peak ~0.7 (2510.00553); update x0.75 +3.4 GSM8K, matched-norm random update 59.5->5% (2610.22438); Olmo-3 RL-Zero leverage 708x random, carried by signs; x1.5 breaks stopping (stop rate to 0.005-0.18) (2610.37719); top 0.1% Fisher mask gives 85% of RL gain vs random 23.9 (2609.36262); RL update is rotation not rescaling, incl. OLMo-3 Think-RL (2609.22146); DARE needs deltas <=~0.002, fails >0.01 (2311.03099); Bolmo moves an Olmo-3 RL-Zero IF delta to a byte model, IFEval 31.1->67.4 (2512.15586); 13 params give 74.6 vs 78.2 full on MATH-500 (2602.04118). Fine-tune sparsity is bf16 rounding, gone in fp32 (2509.04259). (3) Loops: loop onset = entropy drops to ~0 after a Wait/But burst, probe flags 64-76% ~1,500 tokens early (2601.05693); Olmo-3-7B-Think cap hits only 62% loops (2611.06095); loop-neuron edits beat random in 4/8 cells and can turn loops into endless reasoning (2606.13705); repetition-neuron ablation fixes ~30% (2410.13497). (4) Decode-time/steering: SEAL keyword-labeled vector, R1-Distill-7B MATH-500 85.8->89.4 with -21% tokens (2504.07986); proxy-tuning on first tokens only fails (base falls back to repetition) (2401.08565); forced Wait barely moves MATH500 (2501.19393); SAE steering recovers format, not reasoning (2609.15064). items.text: RL gain as context: does a context window carry what the RL weight difference carries? Base + cue, MATH-500, T 1.0/top-p 1.0, grader v3, n 500, same run_cell harness with a longer prefix. Prefix = 3 solved problems from MATH train (none in MATH-500 or the 328), each about 1,500 tokens, in the test template, then the test problem and the cue. Arms differ only in who wrote the 3 answers: (i) cued base, picked without an answer key (4 samples agree, finished), (ii) Math-RL 3.1, (iii) Code-RL 3.1, (iv) control: cued base answers picked at random, same token count. Baselines: base cue 410, theta(0.25) cue 441, RL cue 457. Arm (v), only if (ii) < 441: 16 trainable prefix vectors fit by KL to RL's next-token distribution on RL's MATH-train answers (no reward), as the upper bound of any context. Why: a=0.25 plain (405) equals the cue (410), both RL deltas read out the cue token (result-e2482e), Code-RL gives the math gain with cos 0.014 (result-4b0d5f), and 2505.14216 Table 1 finds SFT on RL's answers gives +11.6 pts while SFT on the base's own correct answers gives +0.8: the gain is in how RL writes, not in correctness. Not tested in context on a base model (Wang 2610.06851 tests only RL's opening of the same problem, 77.7 = cue). Readings: (i) >= 430 is a label-free route with no RL model at all; (ii) >= 441 with (i),(iv) <= 420 means 3 pasted RL answers carry the gain, then run the same 3 answers on a base model of another family that has no RL release; all arms <= 420 and (v) < 441 refutes: context cannot carry it. Generated tokens are equal by design; prompt tokens are reported. Cost: 4 cells, forward only, about 4 USD. Choose on MATH-500, score the best arm once on the 328.

Reward content test: does the MATH-500 gain need a math reward, a reasoning reward, or only RL from the base? AI2 released RL-Zero models from the same base for 5 rewards (names read from HF 02:18 UTC): Olmo-3-7B-RL-Zero-IF, -General, -Mix, -Code, -Math, plus 3.1 Code and Math. We have 2 points: Code-RL cue 450 vs Math-RL cue 457 of 500, weight differences cos 0.014 (result-4b0d5f). Step 1, about 5 cells, 9 USD: IF, General, Mix (and 3.0 Math, Code as same-version controls), cue and plain, MATH-500, T 1.0/top-p 1.0, v3, same run_cell. Baselines: base cue 410, random difference 417, theta(0.25) 441, RL 457. Step 2, forward only: teacher-force base, each RL model, the random difference and theta(0.25) on the same 2,000 stored base answers (job 208b); per token r_m = log p_m - log p_base. Measure the correlation of r across models over positions, and at the 10 percent of positions with the largest |r_Math| whether the other models prefer the same token (2603.22117: replacing those 10 percent of tokens gives the full RL score). Null: the random difference, and Math 3.0 vs 3.1 as the ceiling. Readings: IF cue >= 441 and r_IF agrees with r_Math far above the random null means the gain is the same set of token decisions whatever the reward, so it is a property of the base model, and the next step is to predict those positions from the base alone (label-free). IF cue <= 420 with Code at 450 means the reward must grade a reasoning task. Equal scores with r uncorrelated means different decisions reach the same score. Not published: 2608.03573 reports orthogonal RL updates across tasks and no harm to other tasks, 2509.01363 Sec 4.4 a +2 pt cross-task gain with no control, 2610.24663 and 2603.22117 use one RL model each; none compares token decisions across rewards. items.text: cleanneurons Part T3 (is the RL change a constant push?), Olmo 3 base vs RL-Zero-Math, held-out 2,672 decisive positions after the cue (T1 text / T2 text): adding ONE constant vector per layer to the base (mean of RL-layer minus base-layer output, 32 vectors, no weight change) closes 23.4 / 31.2 % of KL(RL||base); a random vector of the same norm: -1.6 / -4.7 %. A constant on the MLP output only: 14.0 / 15.1 %, i.e. 17-21 % of what all MLP weights close (67.7 / 86.4 %), so 'the MLP change is mostly a constant vector' is refuted. The 472 always-on neurons (0.13 % of 352,256; 110 in the last layer) copied from RL close 2.6 / 3.4 %, vs 0.1-0.2 % for 472 other neurons. Picture: RL = a fixed, direction-specific push per layer (about a quarter to a third) + small input-dependent changes over almost every neuron. Controls passed. Limit: teacher-forced distance to RL, not accuracy. Job sameraslan-1114-184552-a899 (H100, 6 min), commit a2ec2c9. items.text:
Literature sweep 2026-11-15 (work-6b1fa5): 11 pieces read in full by subagents, 45 findings sent to past.dev (tools/paper.py add); texts in papers/<id>.txt. Safety/alignment work excluded. Exa was down (EXA_API_KEY unset), search was plain web. Ranked for the base-vs-RL gap:
1. arxiv-2611.09382 'Exploring Weight-Space Programming' (Shanghai AI Lab, 11-06; NOT an MIT follow-up, an independent replication; code github.com/WSP-Scope/WSP-Scope-Project). One-column edit on Qwen3.5-0.8B: u = normalised (mean embedding of Wait/However/But/Maybe/Perhaps minus mean of Therefore/Thus/So/Now/The/First/Next/Let), layers.23.mlp.down_proj[:,507] -= u. MATH-500 8.35 -> 37.80; on Qwen3.5-9B 97.70 -> 97.35 (no gain where the model does not loop). Controls on 48 questions: base 6, edit 20, column ablation 4, reversed 0, equal-norm random direction 10. Three searches gave +29.45, +5.00, +27.30 points. Proposed: same u from Olmo readout rows, subtracted from the late down_proj columns where the RL delta projects most on u, a in {0.5, 1}, both signs. Refuted if cap hits fall no more than with an equal-norm random direction.
2. arxiv-2608.17124 CASE (08-17): logistic probe on the answer-token residual picks 1 of 4 samples. Qwen2.5-7B MATH-500: within-question AUC 0.763, +2.6 points over vote on hard questions (p<0.001). Needs labels on about 50 calibration questions; a naive probe is at chance within a question (0.502). Proposed: fit on base samples from 100 non-MATH-500 problems, select among our stored 4. Refuted if within-question AUC < 0.60 or it does not beat tie_short 453/500 (pass@4 is 467).
3. arxiv-2607.19331 ISO (07-21): the RL update is rotation of singular vectors, not a change of singular values; remixing inside base subspaces leaves a median 87 % of the update unexplained. Task arithmetic of two RL experts: AIME24 50.83. Proposed: U_RL S_base V_RL^T for Olmo on MATH-500. Refuted if it falls more than 2 points below RL.
4. Goodfire 'Neural Networks Are Already Clean' (10-15, web-785656d81e): neuron-level clamps change looping (zeroing outputs above the 99.9th gate percentile makes Qwen3.6-35B repeat a phrase to the cap). No code. Proposed: set the 50 late-MLP neurons with the largest RL-minus-base change to RL levels in base. Refuted if loop rate moves no more than with 50 random same-layer neurons.
5. 'Sparks of Weight-Space Programming' (web-32b3bf2b22) is the full title of the blog in knowledge-c9fc18; no separate paper. The gain is cap hits only (93.0 -> 33.1 %), so the share of base+cue errors that are cap hits is the ceiling for any loop edit: count it first. The formula W <- W - 6u(u^T W) in knowledge-c1fe13 is not in the blog text.
Lower: arxiv-2509.01363 Reasoning Vectors (GRPO-minus-SFT vector, Qwen2.5-7B GSM8K 55.3 -> 58.9, cue adds on top: 60.3; agrees with our theta result). arxiv-2608.19611 Forking Fast (Goodfire; locates the token where an outcome becomes fixed, code released; use on loop onsets). arxiv-2605.26172 ARBITER (MATH-500 Qwen3-4B vote 69.20, top-2 oracle 76.60; hidden-state rerank and self-review fragile, agrees with result-96e819). arxiv-2607.18100 SOPHIA (loop-exit steering vector, no accuracy reported). Goodfire parameter decomposition (web-4043a8cbfa): 67M-parameter model only, 400,000 steps, not usable at 7B. Goodfire Manifold Steering arxiv-2605.05115: no accuracy evidence.
Not verified: Olmo MLP activation type (decides whether Goodfire's SwiGLU findings apply); no repo opened.

Choose the next interpretability study: 4 proposer subagents (weight-space, activations/neurons, cross-checkpoint transfer, demo-first) each propose studies on the Olmo base vs RL pair, 2 skeptic subagents attack novelty and validity, then one ranked pick with spec outline posted as idea. No GPU.

items.text:
PICK for the next interpretability study (work-3946b0: 4 proposers, 12 proposals, inventory of our own studies, 2 skeptics; both skeptics rank it first): WHAT RL WRITES REGARDLESS OF REWARD.
Claim: RL runs with different rewards (Math, Code, IF, General, Mix, all from allenai/Olmo-3-1025-7B, verified on HF) write the same few singular directions per matrix, and those directions taken only from runs that never saw a math reward give the base the math-RL gain. Refuted if top-8 subspace overlap between rewards is within 3 sd of the random rank-8 null, or the non-math edit scores no better than matched random on hard328 with cue.
Step 1 (weights only, <1 h, ~60 new lines on wsp_delta_anatomy.py, branch claude/weight-space-programming-research-ddd44e): per matrix, mean squared principal cosine between top-8 singular subspaces of each pair of deltas. Start with Math 3.1 vs Code 3.1 (cached). Nulls: random rank-8, Think-SFT delta. Ceiling: Math 3.0 vs Math 3.1. Picture: 7x7 heat map beside its null.
Step 2 (edits, ~80 new lines: a projection recipe in wsp_edit.py with a planted self-test): base + top-8 of IF; + top-8 of General; + Math delta projected on the non-math shared span; + Math top-8 with that span removed; + matched random rank-8; + Think-SFT top-8. First cell ~2 h.
Step 3 (weights only): the same overlap at steps 100/200/400/800 per reward, against a within-reward split-half ceiling: do rewards share an early phase?
Mandatory controls (from our own results): score with the cue on hard328 (base 164, RL 206 of 328; a paired comparison resolves ~5 points), never on plain MATH-500 alone, because Think-SFT with a delta orthogonal to RL scores 91/100 plain and a random delta also gains; same-release pairs (Code 3.0 + cue 411 vs Code 3.1 450); report the effective scale after bf16 rounding (54 % of delta entries are within one ulp); 4 samples per arm where arms differ by under 5 points.
Why novel: published work has whole-update cosines between RL runs (2609.22146: 0.003-0.037), Fisher leverage on the same Olmo deltas (2610.37719), and one-run compact cores (SAR 2607.03065, abstract only). None transfers a subspace from one reward as an edit that gives another reward's gain. Novelty checked from team memory and abstracts, no paper read in full for this.
Why a null is still a result: 'two rewards reach the same gain through disjoint subspaces' resolves the conflict between result-904bbf (change spread over all neurons) and result-d2933e (8 directions suffice).
Depends on work-069eca (reward5 whole-model scores; IF/General/Mix weights cached in abaybektursun's workspace).
Run in parallel, cheap: (a) cue as a one-shot switch: HF generation on 100 plain problems with attention to the cue tokens masked after N = 0/10/50/500 generated tokens, control 3 random prompt tokens masked; plus cosine of the cue-induced residual shift with the RL-induced shift per layer against Code-RL/Think-SFT/random nulls. ~100 lines, first signal ~1.5 h. Refuted if masking at N=50 costs more than 5 points. (b) 20 min CPU: projection of the Olmo late-MLP delta on the 2611.09382 Wait-minus-Therefore direction against 1,000 random word sets, the gate for porting the edit to Qwen3.5-0.8B.
Demo layer once directions survive: a slider on one surviving direction, claim on cap hits and answer length (token-rate change is near-tautological), control = the base's own singular directions at equal norm.
Dropped: RL-at-3%-of-tokens (published: 2603.22117 Fig. 2; our top 4 % of positions hold 39 % of KL), fork autopsy (no prefix mode, 3 h+), Think-DPO transplant (tokenizer differences, GRRR cosines < 0.008), swarm explanations (4 h+ to first signal), bytes curve as a headline (arms differ by 2-4 points).

items.text: Subagents started inside the repository see result numbers that the prompt never gave them: Claude Code puts the 5 newest commit subjects (git status block) into every subagent's context, and our commit subjects carry scores (e.g. 'Day-1 #3 MATH-500 results: base+cue single 405, restart 413, vote4 446 ...'). Found in theory round 02, where a generator reported it; two agents copied their 5 lines on request (studies/theory/results/engine/round-02/exposed.json). Any blind test run through the Agent tool is affected: blind judges, held-out prediction, planted-case reviews. Fix that worked: run the blind call headless from an empty directory outside the repo, 'claude -p --restricted --strict-mcp-config --tools Read,Write --allowedTools Read Write < prompt.txt', with only its input files copied in; its context then has no git status, no CLAUDE.md, no MCP tools (tested; studies/theory/lib/round.py does this for every blind stage). Plain '--allowedTools Read Write' alone does not restrict the tools.

RL-Zero without the reward (plan, not started; riskier follow-up to idea-607778). Thesis: one RL sample is the base's own 4-sample vote paid once in weights. Evidence: RL single 456 vs base vote 446-453 and pass@4 467 (result-5d032f, cbe0bc); the vote adds 8.2 pts to base but 3.6 to RL; the RL delta is 0.24% of weight norm and 8 directions per matrix carry most of it (result-ad3c24). So the reward may be replaceable by agreement among the base's own samples, with truncated answers as negatives (3.0 -> 3.1 added exactly that, and only Code 3.1 transfers to math: 450 vs Code 3.0 411, result-edceef). Stage 0, stored rows, no GPU: among problems where no base sample of 4 is right, how often is RL right; and when the base plurality is wrong, how often RL gives the same wrong answer. Thesis refuted if RL is right on more than half of the pass@4 failures. Stage 1, one GPU job: gradient of log-prob of the stored base samples with sign +1 for plurality-agreeing finished samples and -1 for minority and cap-hit samples; no answer key. Measure its top-8 subspace overlap and cosine with the RL-Math delta against a random null and against the same gradient built with the true key (ceiling). Stage 2: base + one step of that gradient at the norm of 0.25 (RL - base); cue, hard328, vs base 164, theta0.25 182, RL 206. Controls: matched-norm random (417-level null), sign flipped, positives only, true-key. Stage 3 only if stage 2 gains >= 3 pts: on-policy loop on unlabeled MATH-train problems, 4 samples, agreement as reward, rank-8 LoRA, 50-100 steps; first score RL-Zero step_050/100/200 with the cue to see how many steps RL itself needed. Known against it: 2509.04259 (on-policy data matters, not negatives), 2607.13643 and 2505.14216 (SFT on own agreeing or correct answers gives < 1 pt), a wrong plurality gets reinforced. Published neighbour: TTRL uses vote as an online reward; not done from a base model beside a released RL-Zero delta, and no one-step alignment test.

Policy improvement at decoding time, no weights and no reward (plan, not started; riskier follow-up to idea-46b68c). Thesis: what is left of the RL gain is reliability, not knowledge: any of 4 base samples is right on 467/500 (MATH-500) and 205/328 (hard328, = RL single 206), and RL stores in weights the choice a critic could make while decoding. Replace the weights by a critic read from the base's own activations, trained with no answer key (target: will this sample agree with the plurality of 4), and use it to stop a failing sample early and start again. Differs from idea-0d55a4 (vote as a reward for weight updates) and from the length rules (result-2c2cae: +0.9 to +3.7 pts at up to 2.2x tokens): no weight changes, and the critic acts before the length is known. Stage 0, stored rows, no GPU: accuracy and tokens of stop-and-restart with a perfect critic at 10/25/50 % of the answer; stop if it cannot reach 440/500 at <= 1.5x tokens. Stage 1, one forward job: probe on base residual activations at 10/25/50 % of the 2,000 stored MATH-500 samples, 5 folds by problem, AUROC for plurality agreement and (evaluation only) correctness, vs tokens so far, mean log-prob and entropy so far. Stop if AUROC at 25 % is within 0.03 of the best of those. Stage 2: threshold chosen on MATH-500, scored once on hard328 for base and RL with tokens per problem; target base >= 190/328 at <= 1.3x tokens (theta(0.5) 190, RL 206). Stage 3 only if stage 2 gains: at the 10 % highest-entropy positions score the top tokens with the critic and compare the choices with the tokens Math-RL prefers (score_tokens instrument, result-edceef step 2). Against it: result-f21d2e (no J-lens feature beats length for a wrong base answer, AUROC 0.831), 2608.17124 and 2605.09502 (the correctness direction is a readout, steering with it does not help), 2504.05419 (probes for own correctness exist, on trained reasoning models). Checked today on 500 stored base answers: the summed log-ratio log p_RL - log p_base separates right from wrong at AUROC 0.853, the same as length alone (0.855), and the per-token mean does not favour right answers, so the RL model's likelihood is not a usable critic.

items.text: RL's gain on MATH-500 is mostly a reliability shift: 81% of the 198-sample gap (4 samples per problem, n=500, T 1.0, v3; base+cue 1,642 right of 2,000, RL 1,840) sits in problems the base solves at least once in 4; 19% [11, 27] in problems with base 0 of 4. Cell base 3/4 -> RL 4/4: 86 problems = 43% of the gap. Held-out check (class by 3 base samples, score the 4th): the class 'other three wrong' holds 14% [5, 23] of the gap and the base still solves 15% there; in the class 'other three right' the base fails 7.2%, RL 0.9% (43% of the gap). Homogeneous binomial null predicts 0.5 problems at 0/4, observed 33. Only 2 problems go from 0/4 to 4/4 (170, 279); of the 33 base-0/4 problems RL has 0/4 on 16. Level 5 holds 44% [35, 54] of the gap (27% of problems); Intermediate Algebra 30% [22, 39] (19%). Base wrong samples: 250 finished-wrong, 89 cap hits, 19 no answer; RL is right on the same problems 68%, 49%, 83%. Blind judge (Claude subagents with a fixed rubric; no hosted provider key works on this machine) on 60 base / 30 RL finished-wrong: base slip 35% [24, 48], wrong plan 28%, misread 23%, format 13%; RL slip 17%, wrong plan 67%, misread 17%, format 0. Two passes agree on 44 of 45, kappa 0.97 (same model). Controls: shuffled pairs 15/15 mismatch; planted slips 11/15 and 13/15 (misses all labeled format: slip vs format is unreliable for an error in the last line). Base items with a right sibling: 39 of 48 slip/misread/format; without (base 0/4): 8 of 12 wrong plan. About 52 of the base's 358 wrong samples (36 to 79) fail in stating the answer (placeholder left, form rejected by v3, no answer); RL 0. First wrong step at median 0.20 of the answer. Artifacts: studies/rlneurons/results/anatomy/math500-01/ (readout.json, pool_k_le3.json: 183 problems with base k<=3), results/anatomy/judge-01/, README section 'Gap anatomy', spec specs/SPEC_anatomy.md; main aab8649.

Where does low temperature help and where does it loop? (for hard328; config chosen on MATH-500). Facts: cued base at T 0.6 is more accurate when it finishes (378 vs ~362 at T 1.0 on the same 402 MATH-500 problems, knowledge-13cff3) but loops on 98/500; min-p 0.1 at T 1.0 also raises finished accuracy (404/442 vs 410/473) and brings loops back (result-44b4df). Both sharpen every position. Test: a per-token rule in a vLLM logits processor, logits/T_low only where next-token entropy H is above h0 (the top 20 % of positions, 'forking tokens' of 2506.01939), T 1.0 elsewhere; 2x2 with the reverse gate, constant T_low and T 1.0, T_low in {0.6, 0.3}. Hypothesis: loops come from sharpening confident positions (the tail tokens there are the exits from a repeated block), accuracy from sharpening forks. Refuted if the forks-only arm has cap hits at the T 0.6 level, or no more right than T 1.0. Either outcome says which positions carry the T 0.6 gain. Then the winner once on the 328, both models. Not the loop-triggered temperature boost (llama.cpp PR 22007): no loop detector, the gate is the entropy alone.

Entropy-gated temperature idea-069f19: vLLM logits processor (logits/T_low only where next-token entropy is above the 80th percentile, or the reverse), 2x2 x T_low {0.6, 0.3} screen on MATH-500 first 100 (cap hits, loops, right), then the chosen arm on MATH-500 x4 samples and once on hard328, base+cue and RL. RL does not win by checking more: it writes more checking markers (13.1 vs 9.5 per 1k tokens, paired +3.6 [3.4, 3.9], n=500, all of it wait/hmm/actually), but markers do not separate right from wrong samples of the same model and problem (base right minus wrong +0.63 [-0.01, 1.28] per 1k, +0.08 [-0.64, 0.77] at matched length, 150 problems; RL wrong samples have more), the rate after 52 located base wrong steps equals that of right siblings (9.2 vs 9.2; a marker within 500 tokens after 88 % of steps vs 87 % at random positions), and blind judges call 5 of 80 check events a fix (base 3 of 40, RL 2 of 40; kappa 0.88, planted controls 20 of 20 and 19 of 20). 6 of 11 base slips read are followed by a check that repeats the slip. Slip-hazard law for the RL gain: an answer is a chain of steps each with a small chance of an unrecovered slip, P(right) = exp(-h L_i); a method multiplies h by a constant (RL about 0.4x). Test as a complementary-log-log item model log(-log p_ij) = d_i + a_j against the Rasch logit model on the 36-arm x 500 matrix (held out, parametric null, planted power), constancy of each method's hazard ratio across difficulty terciles, linearity of log hazard in theta, transfer to hard328 against point transfer (5.14), d_i against right-answer token length, binomial over-dispersion of the 4-sample outcomes. Activation edits during generation run inside vLLM 0.32 at vLLM speed, no Hugging Face generate needed. vLLM serves Olmo 3 through its Transformers backend, so model.model.layers[l] are the Hugging Face blocks and a torch forward hook on a block acts on every sequence of the batch (hidden state [1, tokens of all running requests, 4096]). Needed: VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0 (model in the job's process), EngineArgs(enforce_eager=True) (a Python hook is not replayed by a CUDA graph), enable_prefix_caching=False when arms differ in activations; find the model by walking the engine's attributes (vLLM freezes the gc list). Per-request logit_bias works with seeded sampling. Instrument check to copy: a huge edit must change every answer (alpha 8 gave only 'wait' tokens). Measured: 17 arms x 63 problems x 1,024 tokens in 11 minutes on one H100; a 500-problem arm at cap 16,384 in 31 to 35 minutes, the same as run_cell; a random direction of 6.8 % of the block norm scores 409/500 (stored unsteered cells 404 to 418). Negative: the cued base's activations do not tell which of its own samples of a problem will fail. MATH-500, 2,000 stored samples (4 per problem, T 1.0, v3), linear probe on the residual stream (layers 12/20/28) after 250/500/1,000/2,000 answer tokens, 5 folds by problem, target with no answer key (sample is in the largest group of agreeing answers). Within-problem AUROC (good vs bad sample of the same problem, 110-137 problems): 0.51 / 0.54 / 0.571 [0.509, 0.634] / 0.51; the same probe trained on the answer key 0.51-0.55; mean log-prob and entropy so far 0.49-0.57. Across problems the probe at the last prompt token predicts the flag at 0.73-0.77: the base encodes how hard the problem is before writing, not which sample goes wrong. Offline stop-and-restart at 1,000 tokens with the probe: 414.1/500 at 4,345 tokens vs one sample 410.5 at 4,008; probe minus random-score +0.8 pts [-0.7, 2.4]. Ceiling with a perfect critic at 1,000 tokens: 438.7 (no key) and 459.2 (key) at about 4,100 tokens, RL single 456. C1-C3 refuted. Checks: exactly 0.500 at the prompt position, 0.49-0.50 with flags shuffled within problems, planted signal found. Limits: linear, one position, 3 layers, n 2,000; a critic that reads the finished answer was not tested. Note for anyone voting on stored rows: comparing extracted_v3 strings splits equal answers (39 % of problems look unanimous); group with rln4_lib.agree. Artifacts: studies/rlneurons/results/critic/{ceiling-02,probe-02}/metrics.json, README section 'Critic at decoding time', branch critic. About 2 USD.

items.text: Slip-hazard law refuted: the hazard (cloglog) item model fits held-out cells worse than Rasch logit, -0.2854 vs -0.2790 nats per cell (T -0.0064, all 5 folds; logit-simulated null -0.0026 [-0.0048, -0.0010], hazard-simulated +0.0031; power 1.0 both ways), 36 arms x 500 MATH-500 problems. RL's hazard ratio is not constant: 0.48 on the hardest 46 problems, 0.23 on the middle 119, 0.11 on the easiest 335 (base wrong cells 157/130/71, RL 117/35/8; hardest minus easiest -1.47 on the log scale, constant-ratio range -0.55 to +0.30). Average hazard ratios vs pooled base + cue: RL plain 0.33 [0.28, 0.40], RL cue 0.37, Think-SFT 0.37, Code-RL 0.44, theta 0.25/0.5/0.75 0.56/0.43/0.43 (log hazard not linear in theta: theta 0.25 has 57 %), base vote over 4 0.51, RL vote over 4 0.60 vs its own samples. Transfer to hard328 (5 arms): same hazard ratio 5.11 problems, calibrated hazard 8.03, point 5.14, logit 5.07: no better than point. Fitted work rises with right-answer tokens (Spearman 0.48 base, 0.59 RL, shuffled +/-0.09) but with slope 0.45 and 0.77, not 1. 4-sample outcomes: bulk variance binomial (D 1.03, 0.90; null 95th pct 1.17), but 8 (base) and 12 (RL) more 0-of-4 problems than binomial and the vote 10 and 9 problems below the independent-slip prediction. Post hoc: the data lie past logit on the side away from the hazard link. Hazard predictions for 5 running cells filed in commit 1da4655 (none finished yet). studies/rlneurons/results/hazard/math500-01/readout.json, table.md; transfer-01/, predict-01/, scored-01/; README section 'Slip-hazard law'; spec specs/SPEC_hazard.md

Arm P = pseudo-reward from the vote, arm G = same with the true key (ceiling). One epoch, hyperparameters of the vote-distillation run (its SFT arms scored 167/168 on the 328, no gain). Score: cue, hard328, vs base 164, theta0.25 182, RL 206. Branch signed.

Do SFT and RL have opposite difficulty profiles? RL removes 89 % of the cued base's errors on easy MATH-500 problems and 25 % on the hardest (result-e41d94); Think-SFT cue (454, no reward) looks the other way round (1.95 logits hardest, 0.61 easiest). Test on stored 0/1 vectors with difficulty defined without the compared arms (MATH level; base-family arms; leave-family-out), same-arm sample pairs as noise floor, 2PL vs Rasch held out, raw rows of Think-SFT's easy errors. If real: a second axis result-5da8a9 could not see, and Think-SFT + RL directions is the stack. Refuted if the SFT-RL profile difference is inside two-RL-sample noise. Laptop only.

Difficulty profile of SFT vs RL idea-095c0d: error reduction by difficulty bin (leave-out difficulty, MATH level) for RL samples, Think-SFT cue/plain, Code-RL, theta blends, top-8, Math 3.0 on MATH-500 stored vectors; 2PL vs Rasch held out; raw rows of Think-SFT easy errors; blind prediction of Think-SFT on hard328 (work-9ecc56). Laptop, branch profile, studies/rlneurons/analysis/profile.py

Is the RL gain practice on its training prompts? 72 of the 400 harder problems are in the Dolci RL-Zero-Math prompts (43 exact, 29 near) and have no T 1.0 score. Score them with 4 samples for base+cue, RL plain, Code-RL cue, Think-SFT cue, and compare with a source-matched unseen set from the 328. D = (RL - control) seen minus (RL - control) unseen. Hypothesis D >= +15 points; refuted if D inside +/-8.

Token frontier: accuracy vs generated tokens per problem for base+cue and RL under reward-free test-time rules (single, restart, vote k=2-4, sequential vote that stops when two samples agree, length-capped sampling), rules chosen on MATH-500 by 5-fold, scored once on hard328. Sequential stopping is published (Adaptive-Consistency 2305.11860, ESC 2401.10480); new here: the equal-token frontier of a base against its RL-trained version. Refuted if no base rule reaches one RL sample (456/500) below the fixed vote's 16,034 tokens.

Seen vs unseen: score the 72 harder problems that are in the RL training prompts (4 samples, T 1.0, v3) on base+cue, RL, Code-RL cue, Think-SFT cue, against a source-matched unseen set; D = (RL - control) seen minus unseen. Branch seen, spec SPEC_seen.md. idea-c1d00f

xreward Part 2, first four cells (hard328 n=328, cue, T 1.0/top-p 1.0, v3, one sample, seed 3000000; edits at 0.074 % of weight norm): the 8 directions and the rest of the RL difference each carry about two thirds of the hard-problem gain, by different routes. Right of 328 and cap hits: base 164, 77; matched random rank-8 158, 67; base + Math 3.1 top-8 directions per matrix 192, 46; Math 3.1 minus those 8 directions 190, 90; RL 206, 20; base + Code 3.1 top-8 178, 41. Paired: top-8 minus random +10.4 pts [5.8, 14.9]; top-8 minus base +8.5 [4.3, 12.8]; top-8 minus RL -4.3 [-8.2, -0.3]; RL-minus-top-8 minus RL -4.9 [-8.8, -1.2]; Code top-8 minus random +6.1 [2.4, 10.1]. Top-8 solves 30 of the 49 problems only RL solved, as does RL minus top-8. So on hard problems the 8 directions are more than the cue (answers the check on result-36e8cd), they are direction-specific, and they cut cap hits, while the remainder raises accuracy and loops more than the base. Raw rows read by a subagent: with top-8, Wait/perhaps/Hmm rates rise to RL's level (Wait 9.2 -> 12.3 per 1,000 words, RL 12.9) and finished answers with no boxed answer fall 22 -> 1. Step 100 (job 221259-0871): each step-100 checkpoint's nearest final model of another run is its own reward's other release or Mix for IF and General (6 of 7; Mix is nearest General), at 0.03 % of weight norm; cross-family overlap 0.076. Artifacts studies/rlneurons/results/xreward/edits/readout.json and run folders, overlap_steps-01/readout.json, spec SPEC_xreward.md amendments 1-3, branch sharedsub. Next: k=1, k=64, attention vs MLP, 2x scale, shared-input-subspace split.

items.text: Olmo-3.1 RL-Zero-Math cap hits at T 0.6 / top-p 0.95 rise early in RL, then fall, and the rise follows the opening, not sharper sampling. Plain MATH-500, sample 0, n = 500 each. Cap hits: base 65, cued base 119, step 100 103, step 400 98, step 2,800 19 (rerun spread 0-4). Theory r4-m10 predicted the rise before the rows were read; both no-theory readers predicted a fall. Step 100: 478 answers have 'Okay' in the first 30 characters (base 193), finished length 2.25 times the base's; at step 400 the cue changes cap hits by -0.028. Median mean_logprob of finished answers: cued base -0.161, step 100 -0.155, step 400 -0.163, step 2,800 -0.192. Steps 100-400 are no sharper per token than the cued base. Reading: the first 100 RL steps install the opening the cue forces. Check on stored rows: step-100 plain accuracy against the cued base's at T 0.6. items.text: Theory round 04 refuted 4 theories by their own computed tests (studies/theory/results/engine/round-04/metrics_v4.json). r4-m02, a longer finished sample reads out failure for the base, not for RL: RL concordance 0.72 (156 pairs) vs 0.55 [0.43, 0.67], above the base's 0.62. r4-m04, base + 0.25(RL - base) draws whole answers from either endpoint: 'Wait'-rate share 0.33 vs 0.76 [0.60, 0.90] plain, 0.21 vs 0.66 [0.44, 0.88] cue, while format share is 0.72. r4-m07, RL keeps the base's repeated wrong answers: 35 of 131 RL wrong answers equal a base wrong answer, 0.27 vs 0.50 [0.36, 0.65]; RL fixes 12 of 16 such problems, 0.75 vs 0.30 [0.12, 0.50]. r4-m09, Code-RL's math gain is only an ending policy: on hard328 it fixes 27 of 90 base finished-wrong problems, 0.30 vs 0.15 [0.07, 0.25], and 10 of 74 base cap-hit-wrong, 0.14 vs 0.33 [0.20, 0.47]. m02 and m09 sit within one standard error of their refuting bounds. Abandoned: m03 (Math and Code RL make the same change), contradicted by result-edceef (Code 3.0 411 vs Math 3.0 448); m05 (gap where the cue fails), by result-fdc8da (121 of 132 'Answer:' answers right).

r4-m08 (theory round 04) lost to its rival: -2.65 nats over two rival turns, 5 tests, every one at or past the rival. The theory: part of the cued base's accuracy is recall from pretraining, so at matched difficulty the RL gap is larger on problems published after the base's cutoff. It survived its own tests on +0.12 nats (post-cutoff excess +6.9 points on 60 problems at T 1.0). The rival (difficulty and termination, no exposure) won: at T 0.6 the excess is -5.6 points on the same 60 problems; RL's own short right answers also have low entropy (0.77, against the base's 0.84); and on short problems both solve, the base's answer length varies more across samples than RL's (0.518, 214 problems), where recall predicted less. No GPU request. studies/theory/results/engine/round-04/metrics_v5.json

r4-m01 (round 04, review: weak) is not separated from its rival: +1.11 nats over two turns (+4.43, then -3.32). The cued base's T 0.6 loops feed on its own text: loop hazard grows with how compressible (zlib) the text so far is. Own tests: +1.41 nats on 3 of 4. For it: within a problem the capped sample's opening compresses better than a finishing restart's in 37 of 46 (theory 0.63, rival 0.53). Against it: where RL's opening is as compressible as the base's, RL's prefix still helps by 0.375 (24 problems; theory 0.12 [-0.07, 0.31]); a more compressible opening does not bring the loop earlier (rank correlation -0.074, 62 loops; theory 0.2). So compressibility marks the sample that will loop but does not explain RL's prefix advantage. Nearest: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.05693. GPU: delete repeated lines from 78 K_own prefixes; 32 [26, 39] finish.

Prefix hand-off, T 1.0, MATH-500 pool of 183 (base right in <= 3 of 4): RL's advantage is in the first half of the answer and is in the text by the halfway point. Base finishing an RL prefix recovers 8.2 [0.5, 16.4] of the 17.5-point own-prefix gap at a 25 % cut, 15.8 [8.7, 23.0] of 19.7 at 50 %, 17.5 of 21.3 at 75 % (right of 183: base own 107/106/100, base on RL prefix 122/135/132, RL on base prefix 131/122/108, RL own 139/142/139). Negative: giving the cued base the RL model's Wait habit does not raise MATH-500 (SPEC3, idea-da9dca, work-74703c). The J-lens direction of Wait/Hmm added to layer 24 during generation until the base writes them at the RL model's rate (8.32 per 1,000 tokens; RL 8.81; unsteered 6.28): 413/500, n=500, T 1.0, cap 16,384, v3. Against four stored unsteered samples (mean 410.5): +0.5 pts [-2.2, +3.1]; against a random direction of the same norm (409): +0.8 [-2.6, +4.2]; RL is 457. Stronger push (alpha 0.1, 11.2 per 1,000): 381, -5.9 [-9.0, -2.9]; 39 answers end without an answer (unsteered 5). Same written rate from layer 20: 398. Logit bias on the six tokens (0.64 nats, 9.72 per 1,000): 421, not below the push (push minus bias -1.6 [-5.0, +1.8]), so the workspace adds nothing over a decoding bias. Why: (1) the push adds the word without a check: a blind reader labelled 16 of 20 push-inserted Waits as filler, 1 as a fix; of the model's own Waits 7 of 20 are fixes; (2) on the 65 problems T1 missed and T2 solved: unsteered 42, random 35, push 35; (3) inside, the push overshoots: hold-on words in the layer-24 readout at 31 % of positions, vs 4.75 % unsteered and 6.29 % in RL; alpha 0.017 already gives 7.2 %. The readout difference is a trace of the habit, not its cause. Caveat: my unsteered arm scored 430 (above the stored 404-418; same sampling path, 48 texts identical to T1); read as a high draw, second seed running. One sample per arm, SD about 7 problems. studies/jspace/results/steer/main-01/metrics.json, readout-01/readout.json, README 'SPEC 3', branch claude/wait-steering-f535b2 1cc3ac8.

So the top-8 input subspaces sit on directions that math-solution text really excites, more for the reasoning rewards than for IF: support for reading the input-side overlap of result-9d979a as a trace of the text a run generated. title: Budget of the cued-base-to-RL gap in four cells: loops replace reliability at T 0.6
what: Fixed rules sort each problem the RL model solves and the cued base misses into loop, budget (cap hit), answer statement, reliability (base right in another stored row) or capability.
why: It shows where the gap sits; at T 1.0 a fresh base sample's gap has RL's budget.
caveat: Gross gaps, one sample per side; hard328 evidence rows weaker (T 0.6, v1); T 0.6 cell graded v1.
Shares (n; loop/budget/answer/reliability/capability; 3 evidence rows): MATH-500 T 1.0 RL 65: 0/.25/.03/.63/.09; theta0.5 53: 0/.21/.04/.64/.11; hard328 Code-RL 37: 0/.27/.03/.43/.27; step 400 T 0.6 66: .44/.12/.06/.38/0; base resample 42: 0/.17/.02/.67/.14. Apart at 90 %: only T 0.6 loop, reliability, capability against each MATH-500 T 1.0 cell, and hard328 capability against RL. Surprise: T 0.6 reliability .38, predicted .15; 9 of its 25 are right answers v1 rejects. studies/theory/results/account/run-02/readout.md (branch theory, a92ae63 and later)

Theory round 05 rival (replaces r5-m03 'top-8 directions = the cue and nothing more'): the top-8 edit of the RL-Math weight change is an incomplete switch per sample. About 85-90 % of base+top8 plain answers follow a weak dose of RL's policy (longer, checking, few quick wrong answers); the other 10-15 % stay in the plain-base register (short, wrong about half the time at any difficulty). Duel on stored MATH-500 rows, 3 of 3 tests favour it, total 8.77 nats against r5-m03: share of top8's wrong problems that the cued base solves 4 of 4: 0.25 (rival 0.27, theory 0.13); mean cued-base solve rate on top8's quick finished-wrong answers: 0.818 (rival 0.76, theory 0.5); share of those with at most 1,000 tokens: 0.773 (rival 0.63, theory 0.4). One rival, 3 tests, not recomputed independently. GPU test, not run (45 min H100): base+top8 WITH the cue on MATH-500; r5-m03 says 425 [412, 438] of 500 (cue redundant); the mixture account expects the cue to remove the plain-register share and score higher. studies/theory/results/engine/round-05/rivals/r5-m03.json, studies/theory/results/engine/round-05/metrics_v5.json

Theory round 05 rival (replaces r5-m10 'two whole answer modes chosen at the opening'): the cue's gain at T 1.0 is robustness to sampling noise. The plain base's terse answers are fairly accurate when cooled and are derailed after the opening by sampled tail tokens at T 1.0; the deliberative register (cued or self-opened) checks itself and survives. Duel on stored rows: turn 1 not separating (3 tests, same predictions); turn 2, 3 of 3 favour it, total 8.84 nats: non-self-opened plain answers with a later 'Wait' or 'Hmm' score 0.075 below cued answers on the same MATH-500 problems (rival -0.14, theory -0.47) and 0.356 above non-self-opened answers without one (rival 0.24, theory -0.03); on hard328 -0.10 (rival -0.10, theory -0.33). Also measured: non-self-opened plain answers gain 0.158 accuracy from T 1.0 to T 0.6. The marker test is a correlation: later self-checks may mark easier problems. studies/theory/results/engine/round-05/rivals/r5-m10.turn2.json, studies/theory/results/engine/round-05/metrics_v5.json

Theory round 05, refuted theories (each by a number computed from stored rows; studies/theory/results/engine/round-05/metrics_v4.json): (1) grader v3 false negatives explain part of the hard328 gap: numeric equivalence recovers 0 of the cued base's finished v3-wrong non-integer answers, gap stays 12.8 points. (2) the cued base overwrites a right first answer: 0 of its v3-wrong MATH-500 answers have a right first marker. (3) base wrong samples are shorter than right siblings on Levels 1-3: they are longer, median log ratio +0.193. (4) the base restates after 'Wait' while RL re-derives: both revise at the same rate, ratio 1.04. (5) Think-SFT fails by cap hits on RL's longest problems: 25 cap hits of 500, and it is 6 problems ahead of RL in the longest quartile. (6) RL step 100 opens with the RL cue: 3.4 % of plain T 0.6 answers open with 'line'. (7) the base boxes a number from the problem statement: base minus RL share -0.043. (8) Code-RL 3.1 wins by code-style work: markers no more frequent than in the cued base, marked answers 0.123 less accurate. (9) RL-only problems are ones the base solves 'a few percent' of the time: per-sample rate is 0.237. (10) Code 3.0 loses long problems through cap hits: 5 cap hits of 500. (11) nothing after the opening adds to the cue's gain: see idea-2f32ff.

what: Tests written by theories before any row was read; the two no-theory readers did not expect the first three.
why: They locate the Code 3.0 deficit by answer length and show the base already solves most RL-only problems sometimes.

Literature for 'RL first installs the cue's opening' and for label-free RL, read 2026-11-15 (findings in tools/paper.py). (1) Per-checkpoint cue curve is unpublished: 2610.24663 Table 3 scores a one-token opening only on base and final RL (Qwen3-4B-Base, AIME: 10.00 -> 13.23, RL 19.32, 35 % of the gain); 2610.06851 App. D Fig. 14 trains RL with the cue forced (reaches plain RL's step-300 accuracy in 100 steps) and Fig. 16 gives opening probabilities before and after RL only. No paper scores plain and cued prompts, or the opening's probability, at intermediate checkpoints of plain RL. (2) Vote-reward RL from a base model is published, without token matching: 2511.04902 Table 1, MATH-500, Qwen2.5 base: 7B 58.2 -> vote 73.6 vs labelled 73.8; 3B 54.2 -> 63.8 vs 64.4; 0.5B collapses to 0.0 vs 33.8. TTRL 2504.16084: Qwen2.5-7B 60.5 -> 80.5. So a no-label reward equals a labelled one when the start model is right often enough, and fails when it is not. (3) Tinker (Thinking Machines) serves no Olmo model; its base models are Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B-Base and Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-Base; its cookbook RL loop defaults to the 9B base, LoRA rank 32, lr 4e-5. items.text: On the 328 the base-to-RL gap is not a selection problem. Vote over 4: RL right and base wrong on 36 problems; the base has a right sample among its four on only 10 of them, none on 26. A perfect selector over the base's four samples (pass@4 = 207) only equals one RL sample (207); the base's vote loses 15 problems to selection, RL's 19. Base-only wins: 7. Neither model: 100 under the vote, 79 with any right sample after restarts. So better voting or tie rules cannot close the gap here; it needs answers the base never writes (weights or longer reasoning: see Think-SFT, cap 32,768). Source: per_problem in studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/hard328_base_cue_s4r2-01/readout.json and hard328_rl_plain_s4r2-01/readout.json (result-5c961a).

title: A slip is chance; a misreading starts before its sentence
what: From the token before a slip the base is right as often as from the start of the problem (49.2 % vs 47.6 %, 21 prefixes); before a judged misreading it has already lost 32 points (32.1 % vs 64.3 %, 14 prefixes).
why: Slips fit a per-step chance of error, so resampling helps them; misreadings are set up earlier in the text than the sentence the judge quoted.
caveat: 51 prefixes, 6 continuations each, cap 4,000 new tokens; from-scratch rate counts the other 3 stored samples within the same token budget.

title: How much the early text depends on the problem tells nothing
what: For the base's 2,000 stored samples, log p(token | problem) - log p(token | no problem) over the first 1,000 tokens ranks the right sample above the wrong one of the same problem in 53.1 % of pairs [46.8, 58.9]; chance is 50.
why: A third label-free early signal fails (after activations 57.1 and the base's own likelihood 51.9), so stopping bad samples early has no working detector; answer length (68.0) is known only at the end.
caveat: 150 problems with both outcomes, 478 pairs. The lowest tenth of the token values reaches 57.5 [51.6, 63.7], the same as the activation probe.
Predictions P1 and P3 refuted: misread samples do not have the lowest value (0.132 nats per token; slip 0.094, wrong plan 0.154). studies/rlneurons/results/wrongstep/probdep-01/, specs/SPEC_probdep.md, README 'Wrong steps'. One 10-minute A100 job on vast.ai.

items.text: Closed routes for 'catch or avoid a wrong base sample while it is being written, no label, no second model' (cued base, MATH-500, all on main, studies/rlneurons README 'Critic at decoding time' and 'Wrong steps'). Early detectors, within-problem AUROC right vs wrong at 1,000 tokens: linear probe on activations 0.571 [0.509, 0.634] (result-b30f15); base's own mean log p 0.519; problem dependence log p(tok|problem) - log p(tok|no problem) 0.531 [0.468, 0.589] (result-f3d708); RL's likelihood of the base text is length only (0.853 vs 0.855). Bound: a perfect detector at 1,000 tokens gives 438.7/500 against 410.5, so even a working one stays below the vote (446). Steering: problem contrast (context-aware decoding) from before the wrong step +1.6 points [-4.2, 7.8], gains above 8 excluded (result-a497ff); T 0.6 raises the wrong steps. What did hold: Math-RL is half as likely to write the base's wrong step (D -0.71 nats); a misreading has cost 32 points before its sentence (result-c495fe); RL capped rows already hold a boxed answer in 69 % of cases, base capped rows in 17 %. Not tested: detectors trained across problems on more data; contrast from the first answer token on a full cell (expected gain under 2 points, below what n 500 resolves).

Null: no two-model relay beats Think-SFT finishing its own answer on hard328 (n 328, T 1.0, v3, 1 sample). Best relay, Think-SFT writes the first 50 % and RL-Zero-Math finishes: 209/328 at 8,923 tokens per problem, vs its control Think->Think 211 (-0.6 pts [-4.3, +3.0]), the stored Think-SFT sample 212 at 10,140 (219 in the other workspace) and RL 206 at 9,315. At 25 %: 207 vs control 219 (-3.7 [-7.6, +0.3]). RL->Think 204 / 199 vs RL->RL 206 / 193. On Think-SFT's 89 cap-hit prefixes RL as finisher has 18 and 17 right, Think 18 and 16: RL ends the cap hits (13 for 96 over the 328) but 59 to 65 of the 89 become wrong boxed answers. Only gain: Think finishing RL's 102 finished-wrong answers at 50 %: 10 vs 4 (+5.9 [1.0, 10.8]), paid with 71 cap hits. Predictions filed first (141c605): H1 refuted as predicted, 6 of 8 arm scores inside the filed ranges. Jobs 6d5e 3d3b 6338 d35a, 5.6 H100-h. title: Handing a Think-SFT answer to RL to finish gains nothing
what: One model wrote the first 25 or 50 % of an answer on the 328 harder problems and the other finished it, for both orders, against each model finishing its own answer.
why: RL stops where Think-SFT would run out of tokens, but it stops on a wrong answer: on the 89 cap-hit prefixes both finishers get 16 to 18 right.
caveat: One sample per prefix; RL finishing its own 50 % prefix scored 193 against 206 stored, so arms are compared with the own-prefix controls.

items.text: Fresh held-out set: does Think-SFT + cue's lead over RL-Zero-Math under the 4-sample vote (hard328: 241 vs 221) hold on competition problems published after the training data of Think-SFT, RL and the base (e.g. AIME 2026, HMMT Feb 2026)? An overlap scan only finds overlap it can match; post-cutoff problems cannot be in the data. Arms: Think-SFT cue, RL plain, base cue, 4 samples, T 1.0, cap 16,384, v3. Refuted if the paired interval of vote Think-SFT minus RL is at or below 0.

Fresh held-out set (problems dated after the training data of Think-SFT, RL-Zero-Math, base): cutoffs from primary sources, find post-cutoff competition set with gold answers, then Think-SFT cue / RL plain / base cue, 4 samples, vote. idea-67db73

Risk-coverage on stored rows (laptop): where does Think-SFT's lead over RL on hard328 sit? Order the 4 samples per problem by label-free signals (finished, tokens, agreement), compare precision at matched coverage for Think-SFT cue, RL plain, base cue on hard328 and MATH-500. H1: lead only in long answers (>12k tokens). H2: RL answers wrong where Think-SFT hits the cap (control: base on the same problems). H3: dropping samples longer than L (L from MATH-500) does not raise RL's or base's vote. Lit (abstracts only, Exa key 401, WebSearch used): 2507.16806 says binary-reward RL is overconfident; no RL-vs-SFT risk-coverage table found.

Risk-coverage of Think-SFT cue vs RL plain vs base cue on stored rows (hard328, MATH-500; laptop, no GPU): precision at matched coverage, by length bin, abstain/wrong/right transitions, length-cut vote with L from MATH-500. idea-ce2272

Think-SFT's lead over RL on hard328 is in long answers only. Keeping each model's shortest answers, precision is equal up to coverage 0.50 (94.8 % vs 93.0 %, +1.8 points [-0.8, +5.5]) and Think-SFT leads by +8.8 [6.4, 12.5] at 0.75 (n 328, 1,312 samples each, attempt 0, T 1.0, v3; base 82.3 % and 63.9 %). Finished answers over 12,000 tokens: right 68.2 % Think-SFT (135/198), 24.4 % RL (87/356), 16.7 % base (41/246); under 12,000 tokens RL has more right samples (706 vs 687). MATH-500: no lead at any coverage. Where a Think-SFT sample gives no answer, RL's is wrong 248 times, right 52. RL's precision on the 141 problems with a Think-SFT cap hit is 31.2 %, against 35.2 % expected from the base's solve rate: mostly difficulty (-3.9 [-6.9, -1.0]). Dropping samples longer than L before the vote (L from MATH-500) does not help: RL 224 vs 221 (+0.9 [0.0, 2.1]), base 189 vs 192. Hand read of 10 long wrong RL answers: 6 box a number the write-up does not derive. Vote check 241/221/192 reproduced. studies/rlneurons/results/riskcov/hard328-01/readout.json, table.md; README section 'Risk-coverage'

title: One cell can now run as N jobs at once
what: run_cell --shard k/N runs problems k, k+N, ... of a set; analysis/shard_join.py joins the N run folders into the folder one job would have written (main 329dd7b, studies/rlneurons/README.md section 'One cell on N GPUs').
why: on a 48 GB GPU the long answers fill the KV cache, 9-12 sequences run and the rest wait (about 200 tokens/s, job ih-1115-092337-b35c: 110 of 500 answers in 23 min). N small GPUs each have their own cache.
Checks: real 2-shard run on two L40S, MATH-500 --n 24: 24 problems, each once, every seed = seed + index, 18 right; laptop dry run, 3 shards = the unsharded run's 22 requests, seeds and prompts; shard_join_test, 7 planted cases (5 must fail).
caveat: not compared row by row with an unsharded GPU run; batch composition differs, so texts can differ as between any two runs. Use: add --shard 0/4 .. 3/4 to the same command, then shard_join --runs <4 folders> --out <name>.
