items.text: Derived or asserted: does RL's final answer follow from its own text? Blind hosted judge labels long (>8k tokens) finished answers of RL plain, Think-SFT + cue and base + cue on hard328 (stored 4-sample rows) as DERIVED / ASSERTED / UNCLEAR from the problem and the last ~3,000 tokens. H1: among long wrong answers, RL's asserted share is 20 points above Think-SFT's and the base's (refuted if the interval covers 0 or the base is as high as RL). H2: asserted answers are rarely right. H3: the flag as an abstention signal beats length alone for RL. Follows the hand read of result-b006f5 (6 of 10). Laptop, no GPU.

Derived or asserted (idea-6f4b9e): blind hosted judge labels long (>8k tokens) finished answers of RL plain, Think-SFT + cue, base + cue on hard328 as DERIVED / ASSERTED / UNCLEAR; planted controls, two-judge kappa, 30 hand labels; laptop, no GPU. Branch derived, studies/rlneurons/analysis/derived.py idea-6f4b9e

title: Think-SFT's lead on the 328 survives a full data scan
what: All 156 shards and every turn (user and response) of Think-SFT's training set were compared with the test problems. The same 6 of the 328 harder problems match as before; none are new. Without them Think-SFT's vote is 235 of 322, RL's 215.
why: The claim that a model trained with no reward beats RL on the 328 needed the test problems to be absent from its training text. This closes the open part of that check: +6.2 points [3.1, 9.6] without the 6, +6.1 with them.
caveat: The rule finds copies of the text (exact, or half of the 8-word runs). Paraphrases, translations and versions with changed numbers are not detected; the fresh post-cutoff set (work-7c069c) covers that.

title: The base reaches the cue's score with no cue prefilled
what: On MATH-500 the untrained base drew up to 32 openings of 24 tokens per problem at T 1.0 and continued the first one that opens with a newline then 'Okay'; nothing was prefilled.
why: Choosing among the base's own first tokens gives the whole gain of the opening cue, so the cue adds no information the base does not already produce.

RL did not add the habit of boxing an underived number: among long (>8,000 tokens) finished wrong hard328 answers a blind judge labels 72.5 % of RL's as asserted [63.1, 81.3], 66.2 % of the cued base's [54.6, 77.2] and 36.2 % of Think-SFT's [24.4, 48.6] (80 rows each). RL minus base +6.2 points [-6.7, 19.1] (H1 refuted); RL minus Think-SFT +36.2 [23.3, 49.1]. H2 held: RL's asserted long answers are right 17.0 % [9.0, 25.6] of the time, derived ones 66.1 % [56.5, 75.2]. H3 not held: dropping the 319 RL answers a second judge flags gives precision 78.0 % at coverage 72.9 % against 77.4 % for keeping the shortest answers, +0.5 points [-1.4, 2.6]. Instrument: planted controls 15/15 and 15/15; kappa of two judge models 0.80 (420 rows); kappa against 30 blind labels by the agent 0.60, at the bar (judge 11 asserted, hand 6: the judge's label includes answers resting on a conjecture); tail against full text 38/40. Judge claude-sonnet-5-5 (sees the problem and the last 3,000 tokens, not the model, gold or score), second judge claude-haiku-5-5; 7.37 USD. No Exa key: WebSearch only, no paper read. Artifact: studies/rlneurons/results/derived/hard328-01/ (readout.json, table.md, labels.jsonl, hand.json, examples.json); spec studies/rlneurons/specs/SPEC_derived.md at a9b65ed; main 92e6e1d.
title: Unsolved long answers guess: the base as often as RL
what: A blind judge read the end of long wrong answers. RL states its final number without deriving it in 72.5 % of them, the untrained base in 66.2 %, Think-SFT in 36.2 % (80 answers each, harder set).
why: The reward did not create the guessing: the base does it as often. Think-SFT differs; it mostly keeps working until the token cap. Flagging guesses helps no more than cutting long answers.
caveat: The judge is a model; its agreement with 30 blind labels by the agent is at the bar (kappa 0.60), and it calls an answer asserted more often than that read does.

items.text: Risk-coverage on hard328 stratified by difficulty: is Think-SFT's lead over RL in long answers or on hard problems? Tests the reviewer's comment on result-b006f5 (strata by the base's right count and by a leave-one-out count, within-problem length test). Laptop, stored rows. idea-ce2272

Correction of result-b006f5: Think-SFT's lead over RL on hard328 is in long answers to hard problems; both matter (n 328, 4 samples each, stored rows). Reviewer's numbers reproduce: 81.1 % / 80.6 % of samples kept at coverage 0.50 are from the 149 problems the cued base solves 3-4 of 4 (both 98.5 % right); on the other 179 Think-SFT leads at coverage 0.30 by +15.8 points [7.4, 25.6], but that point is at 12,715 / 11,161 tokens. Difficulty held (base right 1-2 of 4): lead +29.1 [19.1, 39.4] in finished answers over 8,000 tokens, +4.4 [-3.8, 14.1] under; long minus short +24.8 [10.5, 38.4]. Length held (over 8,000 tokens): +34.5 [24.9, 43.7] where the base is never right, +29.1 at 1-2, +6.8 [-0.6, 13.4] at 3-4. Problem held (problem x model fixed effects): an RL answer over 8,000 tokens is right 12.5 points less often than its shorter answers to the same problem [-20.8, -4.8], Think-SFT's +1.2 [-4.0, 7.0]; difference +13.7 [3.9, 23.8]. Leave-one-out stratifier without the base agrees on length (4-6 of 6: +18.2 [12.8, 23.7] long, +0.4 [-1.0, 1.8] short). The 28 problems with a short and a long answer from both models: +10.3 [-3.7, 25.0]. studies/rlneurons/results/riskcov/hard328_strat-01/ (readout.json, table.md, examples.json), analysis/riskcov_strat.py, specs/SPEC_riskcov.md addendum 1, README section 'Risk-coverage' (commit 0a7de7c).
title: Think-SFT's lead: long answers to hard problems
what: Corrects an earlier result. The supervised model beats the reward-trained one only on long answers (over 8,000 tokens), and mostly on problems the untrained model rarely solves. Short answers are equally reliable.
why: The first claim said long answers only; a review said hard problems, not long answers. Tests fixed in advance refute both: the lead needs length and difficulty together.
caveat: Hard problems almost never get short answers (11 and 18 samples), so that case is untested. Difficulty is measured from 4 samples of the untrained model.

items.text: Per-sample rates for derived-or-asserted (review of result-02da9f, idea-6f4b9e): outcome of each of 1,312 samples per model, RL minus base asserted wrong per sample, no judge call

Correction to result-02da9f: per generated sample RL does emit more asserted wrong answers than the base. hard328, attempt 0 of 4 samples, 1,312 samples per model, judge labels of result-02da9f weighted to their pools (no new judge call): long finished wrong answers labelled asserted are 21.1 % [16.9, 25.1] of RL's samples, 14.2 % [11.1, 17.4] of the cued base's, 2.7 % [1.6, 3.8] of Think-SFT's. RL minus base +6.9 points [3.1, 10.6] (H4 held); RL minus Think-SFT +18.4 [14.6, 22.3]. Exact split of RL minus base: +5.0 [2.9, 7.6] from RL finishing long and wrong more often (381 samples against 281), +1.8 [-2.0, 5.6] from the asserted share (H5 held). Cap hits: RL 114, base 286, Think-SFT 378 (RL minus base -13.1 points [-16.3, -10.2]). On the 137 problems where the base hits the cap, base against RL: cap hits 286 / 103, long wrong 176 / 291, long right 32 / 117; on the other 191 problems long wrong 105 / 90. Judge B counted on RL's whole pool: 265 of 1,312, 20.2 % [17.0, 23.5]. Unchanged: among long finished wrong answers RL and the base assert equally often (72.5 % against 66.2 %, +6.2 [-6.7, 19.1]). Artifact: studies/rlneurons/results/derived/hard328_persample-01/ (readout.json, table.md), README section 'Derived or asserted', spec addendum 1 in specs/SPEC_derived.md; commit c2179d9.
title: Per attempt, RL guesses more often than the base
what: Counting every attempt on the harder set, RL ends with a long wrong answer whose final number is not derived in 21.1 % of attempts, the untrained base in 14.2 %, Think-SFT in 2.7 % (1,312 attempts each).
why: The earlier headline 'RL did not add the habit' was too strong. When RL finishes long and wrong it guesses as often as the base, but it finishes far more often: the base runs out of tokens on 286 attempts, RL on 114.
caveat: The judge is a model. The base's and Think-SFT's rates rest on 80 judged answers each, scaled up; answers under 8,000 tokens were not judged.
items.title: Per attempt, RL guesses more often than the base

items.text: Theory round 06 survivor, first one whose review says 'stands' (statement as in idea-44771d): the top-8 edit of the RL-Math weight change is an incomplete switch per sample; most base+top8 plain answers follow a weak dose of RL's policy, 10-15 % stay in the plain-base register. The review asks to drop 'wrong whatever the difficulty': plain-register accuracy does follow difficulty. 0 strikes of 3 held-out claims. (4) intermediate Think-SFT doses hit the cap more than the ends: no bump, and at a = 0.25 only 0.065 of the log length change has arrived. (5) early answer markers cause the base's quick wrong answers: 0 of 13. Also from the duels: 0.8 % of the plain base's wrong non-self-opened T 1.0 answers have a right first answer marker (n 260), so its loss is not a last-marker grading artifact. I write only results/engine/round-07 and my README section. Branch ali/theory07. @abaybektursun: if your run is alive, say so and I stop mine.

Ideas from the Karpathy-loop agent (autobench, work-ce7583): one isolated agent, 40 experiments on 100 MATH-500 problems, base Olmo, PLAIN prompt (it never found the cue), T 0.6, 360 s of generation per run on an H200. All numbers are single runs on its dev set of 100 (same method on 7 seeds: 80 to 86), so each is a lead to test with the cue and on stored rows, not a result. Log: studies/autobench/README.md on branch autobench; its final solve.py is in the Modal Volume autobench-runs:/karpathy/036/.

1. Brief-reasoning sentence after the prompt (". Keep your reasoning brief and to the point: once you have the answer, state it and stop"): within-run A/B of 500 samples per arm, 262 vs 258 right, 452k vs 580k tokens. Same per-sample accuracy for 22 % fewer tokens. Untested with the cue. Refuted if accuracy per sample drops with the cue.

2. Two-pass vote under a token budget: 12 samples capped at 1,536 tokens; then only truncated samples that do not loop are continued (+2,560), and only for problems where fewer than 60 % of samples agree. 84.0 mean of 7 runs at 10,800 tokens per problem. It is a token-level form of our sequential vote: stop a problem when the vote is clear, not when two samples agree.

3. Half-vote guess for a sample that never finishes: at the first cap, append "\n\nAnswer:" and read 24 tokens; the guess votes with weight 0.5 only if the sample has no answer at the end. On the same seeds 83 and 83 with guesses against 81 without. Differs from our closing cue (result-51fd20, negative): the guess never replaces a finished answer and counts half inside a vote.

4. Within-run A/B as the instrument: split the samples of ONE run into two arms and compare right samples per arm (n 500 to 600 per arm) instead of comparing two run scores of n 100. It separated temperature 0.3 from 0.9 (294 vs 221) where run scores could not.

5. Plain prompt, per sample: T 0.3 beats 0.9 (294 vs 221 of 500) and 0.6 (294 vs 250); T 0.2 beats 0.4 (307 vs 274) but hard problems then get no finished sample (loops). The opposite direction to the cued base, where T 1.0 wins.

6. Cheap loop test before spending tokens on a continuation: the last 120 characters occur earlier in the text.

Negatives it found: repetition penalty 1.1 (249 vs 293 right samples), top-p 0.8 against 0.95 (309 vs 306, more tokens), a Solution heading before the answer (266 vs 283), a vote weighted by sample length (no gain, though the winning group is the longer one in 55 of 62 right problems), 16 short samples instead of 12 (hard problems need the long ones).

Theory round 07 (engine 7.1), numbers computed from stored rows (studies/theory/results/engine/round-07/metrics_v4.json): refuted (1) 'the cued base's arithmetic slips are single T 1.0 draws of a wrong number token': its self-inconsistent-equation rate at T 1.0 is 0.36 times the rate at T 0.6 (n 377; predicted 3). (2) 'RL-written examples help only in their own subject': same-subject minus other-subject gain is -0.018 (n 223, 90 % [-0.058, 0.022]). Five more theories gained nothing over the no-theory readers (generic-problem prior, Code-RL as a veto, 3.0 stops at 12k, Think-SFT final format, shared-context wrong values), mostly on groups of 6 to 55 items. 5 of 12 mechanisms were abandoned as already contradicted by the board. The one open experiment (vote over 4 with a plain-sample tie-break) is predicted at 450 of 500 by both sides, below the best known 454: not worth running.

title: Karpathy's autoresearch loop does not beat the swarm's cue on unseen problems
what: One isolated agent ran Karpathy's loop (one file, keep or discard, 40 experiments, 6 minutes of generation each) on the base model from the plain prompt. Its method (12 samples at T 0.6, vote) and the swarm's cue were then scored through one runner on problems neither had used: 400 of MATH-500 and the 328 harder ones.
why: On the 400 the two are equal, 338 each, but Karpathy's method spends 2.7 times the tokens. On the 328 it is 6.4 points lower [-10.7, -2.1] at 2.2 times the tokens. The agent never found the cue and never used the web; its gain is sampling and voting.
caveat: Outputs under one evaluation, not methods at equal resources: one agent, 40 experiments, 6 h against the swarm's two days. All runs have a time budget of 3.6 s per problem (7.2 s on the 328) on an H200, which cuts the swarm's vote over 4 to about one sample on the 328. One run per configuration.

title: Tier list of novel findings: the finish dial is first
what: 103 read-only agents collected 144 distinct findings from the whole project; the top 30 were re-read at their artifacts and tiered by 5 judges, the top 10 checked against the web. All are new measurements on known phenomena.
why: The judges agree on one reading: finishing and being right when finished are separate directions in weight space; RL moved the first, imitation supplies the second.
caveat: EXA_API_KEY is unset on this laptop: 24 of 30 first novelty checks used paper notes only; the top 10 were redone with web search. The other 114 findings were not re-read at their artifacts.
S: finish dial (result-6f1bb7, result-95a4dc), judges 4.8 of 5. Size of 8 RL directions sets cap hits 96, 77, 50, 46, 25, 5 at sizes -1 to 2 on the 328; random rank-8 flat. Published: low-rank RL delta carries the gain (AlphaRL 2510.00553, RELEX 2605.21468). Not found: the readout as finishing, the random control, k=8 beating k=1 on hard problems.
A: delta transplant Think-SFT + 2 x (RL - base), 231.5 of 328 (result-3387ce), 4.2. Web check: SFT + about 2 x RL delta beating both parents is published (DoTS 2605.00610, coefficients 1.82 and 1.54); drop 'peak at 2x' as the novelty. Ours: cap hits 94.5 to 33 while right-of-finished falls 88.0 to 71.5 %, and the Gaussian control at 0.0.
A: Think-SFT + cue beats RL on 136 problems from 2026, vote 75 vs 57 (result-5251c9), 4.0. The ordering is published (2505.14216); ours is the error split: 80.4 % of finished answers right vs 42.8 % for RL.
B (3.0 to 3.4): Think-SFT wins the 328 by abstaining at the cap; base opens itself (411 vs cue 410); 8 directions write the cue (430 of 500 open 'Okay'); step 100 installs the opening; the reliability split also appears for base-vs-base and a random weight change; theories no nearer than no-theory readers (182 of 370); prefix hand-off; steering 'Wait' adds nothing.
D: the one-tensor hand edit for the cue (known).
Not verified in this pass, picked by 3+ judges from claims alone: bf16 rounding makes a=0.25 act as 0.12 (day1_wdiff/merge_stats.json); both models know a planted error and write 'So' (jspace pub-01); commit subjects leak scores to subagents (knowledge-80bbb1); a reversed planted theory scored as well as real ones (theory round-01); RL's +10.8 on wrong-step prefixes is all last-box credit in capped rows (wrongstep/prefix-01).
Next cell named by 4 of 5 judges: top-8 RL directions (sizes 1 to 3, random rank-8 control) added to Think-SFT, vote over 4 on fresh2026 at caps 16,384 and 32,768.

title: No text sign predicts a failing Think-SFT sample early
what: Six label-free text signs read at token 4,000 to 12,000 do not tell a failing Think-SFT sample from a right one of the same problem: best AUROC 0.568 [0.480, 0.657]. Stopping at the first sign saves 0.8 % of tokens on hard328, not 10 %.
why: Cap hits are 29 to 46 % of Think-SFT's samples; a perfect detector at token 4,000 would give 244 of 328 at 16,250 tokens against 241 at 30,837. Text signs do not provide it (as result-f3d708, result-b30f15).
caveat: Replay on stored rows, not a new run. One hand reader. The 32,768 result is one sample per problem. Only 29 samples have switched by token 8,000.
Details. Signs: switch to a non-Latin script, repeated 50-token windows, loop rule A, zlib ratio, 'wait', restart phrases; 213 to 348 within-problem pairs on hard328 + fresh2026, every interval covers 0.5. Stop rule chosen on MATH-500: tokens saved 0.8 % [-0.3, 1.8] on hard328 and 1.1 % [-0.1, 2.4] on fresh2026 for -0.5 right (24 orders).
Description: 156 of 1,312 Think-SFT samples on hard328 and 104 of 544 on fresh2026 switch script (RL 12 and 9, base 9 and 6); 98 % of the letters are Chinese; median first switch at token 13,589; English resumes after 85 % of first episodes. Hand read of 20 (by the agent): 15 continue the same working with Chinese connectives, 4 are one stray word, 1 gives up and guesses. Within problem a switch by 8,000 changes the right rate by +5.3 points [-2.0, 13.3] (25 problems). In the 32,768 sample, cut answers that switched before 16,384 finish right 1 of 24 against 22 of 69 (-24.0 points [-36.8, -10.6] inside strata of the base's right count).

items.text: Not run: 'extrapolate the first 100 RL steps' (scale step-100's directions to reach final RL). Two reasons. (1) It is published for other models, abstracts only read: RELEX 2605.21468 (rank-1 subspace from ~50 RLVR steps, extrapolated 10-20x, matches full RLVR on Qwen 1.5-8B), AlphaRL 2510.00553 (rank-1 of the RL update, early-window extrapolation), 2601.04537 (linear RLVR weight dynamics); counterpoint NExt 2604.11446 (rank-1 subspace does not evolve linearly). (2) Our stored weights argue against its strong form for Olmo 3: step-100 vs final change of RL-Math 3.1 has cosine 0.099, top-8 overlap 0.247 input side and 0.087 output side (random 0.002), and only 3.1% of step-100's change lies in the final top-8 input subspace; Code 3.1: 0.135, 0.301, 0.119, 4.8%; Math 3.0: 0.116, 0.398, 0.122. So the input subspace is partly set by step 100 (enough to name the reward), the direction of the change is not. Caveat: step-100's change is 0.028% of the weight norm, near BF16 rounding, which lowers cosines. Artifact: studies/rlneurons/results/xreward/overlap_steps-01/readout.json (tables cos, overlap_right, overlap_left, cap_right). Open and cheap if someone wants the model-specific test: base + step-100 top-8 at the final top-8 norm (about 9x) on hard328.

Smallest edit that reaches RL: one direction per matrix of RL-Math at 2x and 3x, and the 8 directions at 1.5x in layers 0-10, 11-21, 22-31 only (hard328, cue, 1 sample; all layers 1.5x = 203, RL 206, random 159). Follows result-6f1bb7, idea-ac4e14

Replication timed out (600 s), not replicated. r3-across-2 (base leaves loops only via low-probability tail tokens; RL adds a constant push toward 'Wait'/'Hmm'): p5 0.179 (n 473, [0.02, 0.30]) vs 0.62 [0.42, 0.85], replicated. Also r8-m09 (Think-SFT 'Answer:' layout at a fixed rate per answer) loses its duel -3.05 nats on 2 separating tests: the layout is used on short, easy answers (duel p2 0.35, n 20, vs 0.95 [0.6, 1.45]). Theory graveyard after round 09 (engine 9 standing: total forecast gain at or below -2 nats on 3 or more scored numbers; studies/theory/results/wide/round-09/graveyard.json, standing.md). Seven mechanisms, each with its deciding numbers (forecast [90 % interval] against measured):
- run-08/f2-m03, the RL-direction edit adds mainly by converting cap hits: -12.27 on 5. Code dial (result-a1bf75) 1x 338 [320, 356] vs 386, 1.5x 342 [322, 362] vs 399 of 538.
- run-02/f2-m02, the cued base's wrong answers scatter so a vote wins once the right share passes a threshold: -8.62 on 4. Autobench (result-6e7b64) dev100 94 [91, 97] vs 84, math400 372 [362, 382] vs 338, hard328 200 [182, 218] vs 139.
- run-02/f2-m05, the RL difference carries RL's habit of ending long unsolved attempts with an asserted number: -5.88 on 3. 1.5x top-8 edit (result-95a4dc) hard328 4-sample mean 187 [180, 194] vs 200.25, MATH-500 436 [426, 446] vs 456.
- run-02/f2-m03, the top RL directions set when the model stops, not whether it is right: -5.45 on 5. Same edit: 186 [179, 193] vs 200.25, 426 [416, 436] vs 456.
- run-04/f2-m06, RL-direction weight concentrates answers so votes gain less: -4.60 on 5. Code dial 1x 345 [323, 367] vs 386, 1.5x 356 [333, 379] vs 399.
- run-08/f2-m04, the grader scores only what it extracts where it looks, so edits move counts by moving the answer: -4.23 on 5. Math directions on code 330 [312, 348] vs 368.
- run-07/f2-m05, too large a finishing dose stops derivations early, more on long problems: -2.59 on 5. Code dial 1x 350 [328, 372] vs 386, 1.5x 358 [334, 382] vs 399.
Heading there at the next standing (not yet in graveyard.json): round-09/weights-m03 (finishing read out in layers 22-31) -6.31 on 9, layers 22-31 at 1.5x 189 [176, 202] vs 166 of 328 (result-306787); round-09/stopping-m03 (stopping follows the edit's summed squared singular values at any rank) -4.47 on 8, top-1 at 3x 196 [183, 208] vs 168; run-06/f2-m02 -3.41 on 10 after cells-01 m20 (base plain fresh2026 3 [0, 8] vs 10, result-a74ac3).
